A voice-link capture endpoint cannot be wrapped in the conversion plugin the single selected-microphone name is built on -- it fails with 'Poll FD initialization failed', because the plugin does not hand a forwarder the poll descriptors a capture needs -- and the endpoint exists only while the link is up and is named after the headset's own address, so nothing downstream could open it by name and survive. The call supervisor therefore owns the radio end and writes into a loopback substream, which is exactly the shape the echo canceller's output already has. A LOOPBACK CAPTURE WITH NO WRITER WAS BELIEVED TO BLOCK RATHER THAN RETURN SILENCE, and a 'silence pump' feeding it zeros was built on that belief and then retired the same day. Measured on the panel 2026-09-19: with nothing writing, the name delivered ten seconds of exact zeros; a forwarder in the real leg's shape ran twelve seconds with no error; and a reader held across a writer arriving and then leaving -- a call starting and ending -- survived both transitions with an empty log. The loopback's capture side free-runs on its own timer, so the silence is the loopback's own and nothing maintains it. The pump is recorded here because it also required the supervisor to sequence two writers onto one substream, and because a component whose stated reason is false is worse than no component. Naming the panel's own capsule there instead was refused: it would tunnel a microphone the Owner believes is switched away from, which is the one failure in this design nobody in the room can hear. THE MUTE REACHING BOTH CAPTURES is review finding 1 of 2026-09-19: the bridge opened the headset's microphone before consulting the mute, on the reasoning that the gateway-bound leg is the one that sends. A microphone this panel has opened against a mute is a privacy failure whatever happens to the samples afterwards.
AcceptanceCriteria: Policy tests cover the source selection in every switch position, the input mute stopping both legs while leaving the output legs running, the output Mute position ALSO muting the microphone (item J) and refusing an independent unmute while it is selected, and a selected-but-absent headset routing nothing at all. Generated-file tests assert the microphone on the rear pair only, an explicit zero on every other channel, the complementary zeros in the speaker route, and that the two tables' owned channels are disjoint and together cover the whole map. Applier tests assert that only the rear pair of the adapter's eight hardware levels is moved and that an unreadable control moves nothing, that the rear level returns to silence when no leg runs, that a changed selection restarts the legs rather than starting them, that a mic leg's failure does not fail the apply while an output leg's does, and that the leg is refused while the speaker chain has fallen back to its exclusive stereo open. Knob tests assert refusal rather than clamping, that a refused value in a command moves nothing at all, and field-by-field fallback of a damaged file. Supervisor tests assert that only a synchronous-connection playback endpoint counts as a call, that a call in progress is never moved to another device, that an unreachable daemon means no call rather than an open microphone, that the poll interval is clamped, and that a rollback out of bus mode stops the leg. Configuration is parsed by alsa-lib itself: every name resolves, and removing either generated file costs only that file's name. Unit tests assert no mic leg is enabled and both carry the mode gate. Call tests assert that the incoming direction is off unless its knob is set, that an object published for a connected device is not treated as a call while its PCM reports itself not running, that the outgoing leg keeps its fixed rate while the incoming leg opens at the rate the link negotiated, and that a running PCM which will not state its rate is dropped rather than guessed. Mute tests assert that the input mute stops the outgoing leg alone, within one tick, leaves the incoming leg running, and that the unit is not one of those the applier stops for a mute. Observable tests assert the published document's shape and permissions, that its revision counts events rather than polls, that it carries aliases only and null for an alias that cannot be resolved, and that every read or write failure answers 'no call' while the audio keeps running. Source tests assert the third source is named in the Headset position whenever it resolves to Bluetooth, that it is a loopback and never a radio endpoint in any generated configuration, that the substream it uses is one the loaded module actually offers, and that no silence writer exists -- the loopback's own free-running silence is what the position carries, and the retired pump may not return without the three measurements that retired it being repeated. Supervisor tests assert that no path opens the headset's capture without the mute having answered first, that a mute arriving mid-bridge stops both captures within one tick, and that the far end stays audible throughout.
Permutations: source={panel,headset}; output={mute,headset,speaker}; input_mute={on,off}; headset={present,absent}; speaker-chain={multi,stereo}; sco={absent,one,two,lost}; mic-file={present,absent,damaged}; knob={in-range,out-of-range,unknown,malformed}; mic-source={panel,headset,clean,bt}; resolution={bluetooth,usb,none}; bt-mic-writer={bridge,none}

Title: Panel presentation and thermal telemetry collector
Requirement: The wall image shall run a local collector that samples, on a monotonic five-second schedule with UTC timestamps, every readable thermal zone and hwmon sensor it inventoried, whole-system CPU utilisation derived from counter deltas, and the renderer's own validated presentation snapshot (FULL or TABBED, selected tab, actual fullscreen owner, selected media preference, actual visualiser status, display power and music activity). It shall write a versioned JSONL schema carrying units, session and boot identifiers, rotate it under a seven-day retention and a 50 MiB hard cap, and expose a documented local export. A missing sensor shall be recorded as unavailable and never as zero; an initial CPU sample with no valid delta shall be unknown; a stale or absent renderer report shall be unknown and never logged as the current mode. Sampling or logging failure shall not block input, audio or rendering, and the collector shall not wake a suspended panel but shall identify the gap on resume. The renderer's snapshot shall be written to a run directory the unprivileged panel user can actually write.
Rationale: Plan item S. The panel's heat behaviour is the open question that gates the item Q ProjectM trial, and the trial is only meaningful if the log distinguishes the mode that was ACTUALLY on the glass from the remembered tab and the requested preference. The renderer snapshot moved to /run/wall-panel-renderer because /run/wall-panel is root-owned 0755 and the panel user could not write into it, which made the whole path fail silently; the application payload and the system payload must therefore ship together.
AcceptanceCriteria: Unit tests cover the sampler's counter-delta arithmetic, the unknown-until-a-valid-delta rule, unavailable sensors, alternate labels for one sensor not being double counted, rotation and the size cap, a clock jump, and a suspend/resume gap. Install tests assert the unit file is staged, installed, daemon-reloaded, enabled and started by firstboot, and that the tmpfiles fragment creates the renderer run directory with an owner the panel user can write as. Records are shown to differentiate Tabbed/Pandora from Fullscreen/Door and to carry mode-change entries for transitions shorter than one sample interval.
Permutations: sensors={present,absent,duplicate-label}; cpu-sample={first,delta,counter-reset}; renderer={fresh,stale,absent}; disk={ok,full}; lifecycle={start,restart,suspend,resume}; retention={under-cap,over-cap,over-age}

Title: ProjectM preset payload as a declared deployment dependency
Requirement: Where the opt-in ProjectM ambient visualiser is offered, the wall image shall carry its preset set as a hash-pinned payload reproduced from a committed lock file, install it to a documented location with recorded ownership and modes, and declare it in the release dependency manifest. A payload whose locked entries are absent or whose hashes mismatch shall fail the build and refuse the deployment rather than install partially. An EMPTY lock shall be reported as the deliberate unruled state -- no preset pack has been licensed and chosen by the Owner -- and shall not be presented as a successful install.
Rationale: Plan item Q. The upstream Milkdrop packs carry no licence, so the set is an open Owner ruling and the lock ships empty on purpose; the renderer is built to run presetless. The requirement exists so that the day a set is ruled in, the payload has a declared install transaction instead of a README claiming an installed location that nothing creates -- the state this row was written to correct (terra 2026-09-14, finding 5).
AcceptanceCriteria: The builder reproduces every locked file by SHA-256 or fails hard; an empty lock exits with the deliberate-state message and installs nothing. Install tests assert that a non-empty payload reaches the documented location with the recorded owner and modes and is named in the manifest, and that a removed or mismatched file is detected and refuses activation rather than being ignored.
Permutations: lock={empty,populated}; payload={present,missing,hash-mismatch}; install={fresh,repeat,removed-upstream}

Title: Responsive grid-stepped rocker with guarded apply
Requirement: The wall image shall move the physical-rocker volume by exactly one five-percent step per firmware break pulse, shall publish a bounded read-only absolute preview of the gesture that advances with those pulses and terminates explicitly, and shall apply each movement as an absolute compare-and-set against the audio mode, output, level and state revision it was computed on.
Rationale: Owner ratification 2026-09-16 (end-of-gesture rounding visibly took levels back) as amended 2026-09-18 by the strategy B selection: the 2026-09-18 kprobe capture at serio_interrupt proved the ~106 ms repeat is the firmware re-sending make/break pairs, so there is no held-duration to integrate and the pulse count is the specification. One apply costs 498-551 ms, so the overlay and the audible level must be driven by separate, bounded mechanisms rather than by one blocking loop.
AcceptanceCriteria: Tests cover one/many/reversed pulses, the gap adding no step, boundary clamping and pulse conservation (98 up down = 95), the exact preview schema and every terminal phase, a guard refusal after an output or state-revision change, an ambiguous verdict, and a bound of one active request plus one replaceable target.
Permutations: pulses={1,2,many,reversed}; volume={grid,off-grid,boundary}; preview={active,settled,refused,cancelled,stale,malformed}; guard={holds,output,level,revision,mode}

Title: Per-connection volume-apply health
Requirement: The wall image shall report each wall-volume-request@ instance's exit status from the request apply, not from delivery of its verdict to a local peer. A peer that closes before sending a request shall make no change, journal one line and exit zero; once a request has been read, an undeliverable verdict shall preserve the apply result; and an unreadable partial request shall still fail. The request parser contract is unchanged: handle_request(b'') continues to return error and applies nothing. The template unit shall collect inactive and failed spent instances.
Rationale: A per-connection unit red solely because its reply peer left makes systemctl --failed unreadable and hides real failures. This is deliberately not a widened request boundary: EOF before a request is a transport no-op, whereas an empty request delivered to the parser remains invalid.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_panel_volume_keys.py:test_connect_and_close_is_not_a_failure_sr028, test_an_undeliverable_verdict_reports_the_apply_not_the_delivery_sr028, test_an_undeliverable_verdict_still_reports_a_failed_apply_sr028, test_a_request_that_cannot_be_read_is_still_a_failure_sr028 and test_spent_instances_collect_themselves_sr028 prove the five outcomes. The unit declares CollectMode=inactive-or-failed.

Title: Capability-led weekly filesystem trim
Requirement: The hub shall replace the stock weekly fstrim command with a wrapper that enumerates real mountpoints, deduplicates them by source and consults each source device's advertised DISC-MAX capability. A source advertising DISC-MAX 0 is skipped with a printed reason; an absent or unparseable DISC-MAX answer is treated as no discard support and skipped with a printed reason; every other source is trimmed with stock fstrim options; an empty real-mount list succeeds; and a trim failure on an advertised-capable device exits non-zero. The fstrim.service drop-in shall reset ExecStart before adding the wrapper so the stock and wrapper commands cannot both run.
Rationale: /srv/library and /mnt/backup-drive are non-discarding spinning USB disks, but path exclusions would fail on a future mount layout. DISC-MAX is the device's own answer. systemd ExecStart is list-valued, so a drop-in without an empty reset silently retains the failing stock command.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_homehub_fstrim.py:test_a_clean_run_trims_the_discardable_and_skips_the_rest, test_a_skip_is_never_silent, test_a_device_that_advertises_discard_and_then_refuses_is_still_a_failure, test_one_device_is_asked_once_however_many_times_it_is_mounted, test_a_device_lsblk_cannot_describe_is_skipped_rather_than_assumed and test_nothing_mounted_is_not_a_failure prove the wrapper outcomes and staged drop-in reset.
Permutations: mount={real,pseudo,empty}; source={unique,duplicate}; discard={zero,advertised,absent-or-unparseable}; fstrim={success,failure}; drop-in={reset-present,reset-absent}

Title: Desktop S/PDIF retry preserves systemd start-limit protection
Requirement: The wall image shall configure wall-spdif-in.service with a bounded geometric restart delay for its external desktop S/PDIF capture source: it shall retain Restart=always and the existing StartLimitIntervalSec and StartLimitBurst, begin retrying at two seconds, progress through six restart steps and cap the delay at 120 seconds. The schedule derived from the unit's own values shall permit fewer starts than StartLimitBurst inside StartLimitIntervalSec, so a temporarily absent desktop clock cannot exhaust the limit while a genuinely hard-failing unit remains protected.
Rationale: S/PDIF capture opens only while the desktop source supplies a clock. Its temporary absence is normal during desktop sleep or idle output, while a panel-local leg failing to open is not established as the same condition. The 2026-09-15 flat retry hit the start limit; the desktop awake on 2026-09-16 opened cleanly.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_wall_audio_switch.py::test_the_desktop_leg_backs_off_instead_of_exhausting_its_start_limit_sr028 derives systemd's schedule from wall-spdif-in.service and proves fewer starts fit in the configured interval than the configured burst limit. It does not freeze implementation constants beyond the requirement's stated policy.
Permutations: source={desktop-awake,desktop-sleep-or-idle}; failure={brief,xrun,persistent}; retry={initial,ramped,capped}; start-limit={preserved,hard-failure}

Title: USB audio and relay re-enumeration recovery
Requirement: The wall image shall recover the configured audio switch and LCUS-2 amplifier actuation when the 0d8c:0102 adapter or 1a86:7523 relay re-enumerates. The adapter udev rule shall directly activate only non-switch-policy consumers and shall invoke one non-RemainAfterExit reassert of apply-state for all switch-dependent legs. apply-state shall log and succeed without issuing mixer or unit commands when the configured adapter is absent, but shall preserve failure reporting when it is present. The relay shall have a stable systemd alias and add activation; the actuator service shall want and order after that alias without binding its lifecycle to it.
Rationale: A manually maintained udev leg list already omitted bus-mode legs once, and the boot applier waited 45 seconds for hardware that appeared twenty seconds later. The relay is a separate actuator: its absence must be visible and recoverable but must not stop the audio graph.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_wall_audio_reenumeration.py derives every adapter BindsTo unit from unit files and requires direct udev activation or policy.ALL_LEGS ownership; it also inspects the non-sticky reassert and relay alias/order. tests/test_wall_audio_switch.py exercises absent-adapter apply-state as a successful deferral.
Permutations: adapter={present,absent,re-add}; leg={direct,policy-owned,unowned}; mode={trigger,panel,bus}; relay={present,absent,re-add}; apply={success,real-failure}

Title: Removable audio hardware defers deployment without hiding switch or daemon failures
Requirement: The wall image shall treat an absent configured USB audio adapter as a deferred wall-audio-mode apply: it shall publish a consistent requested mode file and selected ALSA-chain symlink, issue no mixer or unit commands, log the deferral and exit zero. Publishing the selection is a precondition of the deferral, not an accompaniment to it: if the pair cannot be published the command shall restore the previous selection and exit non-zero, and shall report a failed restoration distinctly, because a symlink and mode file naming different modes is the one state no later reader can reconcile. A present-adapter mode switch that records any operation failure shall remain non-zero. When panel-amp-trigger receives SIGTERM or SIGINT after it has started, it shall attempt to record a safe relay OFF and exit zero only when the relay device node is absent; an unverified OFF against a PRESENT relay shall remain non-zero, as shall configuration and unsafe-start failures before a termination request.
Rationale: A removable device being out is normal during wiring and re-add policy already recovers it. A failure after the graph has begun changing is different: its half-applied warning prevents two chains driving one adapter. A BindsTo stop is likewise intended systemd lifecycle, not evidence that the relay daemon independently failed.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_wall_audio_mode_selection.py EXECUTES set_mode_selection and require_mode_selection against a temporary tree, forcing publish and rollback failures, and is mutation-checked against both; tests/test_wall_audio_switch.py holds the deferred branch to the checked call and the retained fatal counted-failure path. tests/test_wall_amp_trigger.py drives SIGTERM through the relay-absent running loop and separately proves unsafe startup stays fatal. TC-953 remains a panel firstboot demonstration because no hermetic firstboot harness exists.
Permutations: adapter={present,absent}; mode={trigger,panel,bus}; switch={deferred,operation-failure}; relay={present,absent}; termination={SIGTERM,SIGINT,none}; daemon={requested-stop,unsafe-start}

Title: HEVC decode-profile proof at wall firstboot
Requirement: The wall image shall install the VA-API inspection dependency and at firstboot make a non-fatal check for `VAProfileHEVCMain : VAEntrypointVLD`. On success it shall log the driver version; on a missing profile it shall warn that H.265 frames may be black while the rest of the panel continues; and when vainfo is unavailable it shall say the check did not run. The image's declared capability and OfficeWallNaglight's Electron decode-enabling feature switches form IF-019.
Rationale: A healthy kiosk can otherwise show a black frame with no direct fault. The profile establishes hardware/image readiness but does not admit HEVC into Electron; the shell switch is an independent, required half of the same user-visible capability.
AcceptanceCriteria: Tests to be added assert the success log includes the driver version only with the HEVC Main VLD profile, the missing-profile path is a loud non-fatal warning, and absent vainfo reports an unrun check rather than a pass. Interface inspection asserts the counterpart's two required Electron switches are named.
Permutations: vainfo={present,absent}; profile={HEVC-Main-VLD,missing}; result={pass,warn,unrun}; shell-switches={both,GL-only,neither}

Title: Bounded merged-bus visualizer telemetry and the optional ProjectM PCM stream
Requirement: The wall image shall run one least-privileged wall-bus-visualizer.service which opens ALSA `bus_monitor` through `arecord` at S16_LE, 48000 Hz, two channels and 1024-frame periods, and fans each captured block into (i) a bounded derived document at /run/wall-bus-visualizer/bus-telemetry.json and (ii) an OPTIONAL bounded local PCM stream that exists only while an authorized local client is attached. The document shall be schema 2 with source `bus_monitor`, carrying bounded RMS, peak, eight band scalars, an activity boolean, the producer's own monotonic observation instant and a capture generation, and shall distinguish an unavailable producer from observed silence. `bus_monitor` is declared in asound-bus-mode.conf alone, so in every other ALSA mode the service shall publish unavailable rather than open a device, and the panel shall render that differently from silence and fall through to Frame Media. The broker's switch backend shall consume this document in place of the `speaker_tap`-derived one, shall AND its activity with the confirmed output selection in /etc/wall-panel/audio-state.json so that Mute reports inactive without claiming the capture is gone and Headset visualizes, and shall not let a microphone reading stand in for an absent bus: a bus that publishes nothing usable shall be reported unavailable whatever the microphone is doing. The optional `microphone` block SHALL remain in the reply for its own consumer -- the microphone button's level ring -- and shall never contribute a band, an activity claim or an rms/peak value. Raw samples shall not be retained or emitted unless explicitly permitted: the one permission is ProjectM's, it is local and memory-only, it holds only while ProjectM is the selected and visible fullscreen owner, and the samples shall never be written to disk, journaled, included in diagnostics or telemetry, uploaded, or retained after ProjectM yields. That exception grants no microphone capture, no recording, no diagnostics and no network transmission. The PCM endpoint shall be AF_UNIX only, mode 0660, authorized by peer credential and filesystem permission, shall keep at most one unsent block per client and drop the older one under backpressure, and shall close and discard its buffers on disconnect, capture failure, mode change, suspend and service stop. The amplifier detector shall continue to read `speaker_tap` and only `speaker_tap`, and no failure of this service shall alter routing, the switch or the relay.
Rationale: The merged bus is the only signal that covers both audible destinations, and the post-switch tap the visualizer used is the detector's signal for a different job. Being pre-switch is what makes the confirmed output selection part of the decision rather than a detail. Keeping the capture out of the broker preserves the SR-023 boundary: the process the renderer talks to still cannot open a sound device. A one-block latest-wins stream is enough for a live decoration and structurally cannot accumulate a recording. Peer credential plus the socket's own permission answers the Owner's stated household threat model and is not offered as protection against a compromised host or home network.
AcceptanceCriteria: Unit tests prove the frozen frame round-trips and refuses every malformed, truncated and oversized shape; that the window is bounded, normalized and aimed at its declared band centres; that the document is schema 2, names `bus_monitor`, carries no samples, and publishes zeros rather than the last frame whenever it is not measuring; that unavailable, silent and stale are three distinguishable answers; that the backend refuses a version-1 `speaker_tap` document outright, ANDs the confirmed switch position, and treats an unreadable position as not-audible; that an absent, malformed or unavailable bus reports unavailable even when a microphone is publishing, and that a loud microphone over a silent bus still draws a quiet room while its own level is reported beside it; that Headset visualizes and Mute reports inactive while the bus stays live; that an empty allow-list denies; that the queue is one deep and drops the older block; and that every teardown path closes the stream and clears the buffer. Failure isolation is proved by injection rather than asserted: a telemetry write failure is survivable, an unframeable block drops the streams instead of guessing, and the shipped detector names neither the new document nor `bus_monitor`. A Linux socket test proves the 0660 mode, the peer-credential refusal and a real frame reaching an authorized peer. Physical acceptance of each source, the Mute behaviour and the ProjectM teardown on the wall remains open.
Permutations: mode={bus,trigger,panel,default}; capture={live,silent,refused,ended}; output={speaker,headset,mute,unreadable,sparse}; document={valid,absent,malformed,oversized,stale,version-1}; peer={permitted,other-uid,none,empty-allow-list}; frame={valid,bad-magic,bad-version,bad-header,truncated,payload-mismatch,oversized}; queue={empty,one-block,slow-consumer}; teardown={disconnect,write-failure,mode-change,capture-failure,stop}; relay={normal,visualizer-failed}

Title: Outbound-initiated remote access and LAN subnet routing
Requirement: The hub shall run one outbound-initiated mesh-VPN daemon installed from the vendor's APT repository as a host service, not as a compose service, and shall advertise the LAN CIDR as a subnet route so that clients reach LAN-only hosts which will never run a tunnel client. It shall enable IPv4 and IPv6 forwarding through a dedicated sysctl drop-in. It shall NOT be configured as an exit node. It shall accept no inbound port: the daemon dials out, and no router forward, firewall rule or published container port shall be added for it. Authentication shall be interactive at first bring-up and no reusable auth key shall be written to the repo, the image payload or the secret store. The node shall be brought up with acceptance of the tunnel's DNS disabled, because Technitium is this LAN's resolver and a second resolver injected onto the hub would displace it. THE COORDINATOR-SIDE CONTROLS SHALL BE ENFORCEABLE ARTIFACTS AND CHECKS RATHER THAN DOCUMENTED INTENTIONS: a tenant ACL shall exist as a tracked, reviewable file in this repo and shall not be an allow-all policy; the converge path shall QUERY tailnet-lock state rather than assume it, and the health check shall FAIL when the tunnel is authorised while lock is disabled, and shall FAIL when more than one node exists while the ACL artifact is absent. The identity account's multi-factor property cannot be observed from this box and shall NOT be asserted by any test; it is recorded as an operator attestation in the runbook. Caddy's LAN_CIDR gate shall additionally admit the tunnel's address range, and that range shall be scoped as narrowly as the tunnel's addressing permits rather than admitting the whole shared carrier-grade-NAT block, because that block is not exclusively this tunnel's. The router's WireGuard server configuration shall be retained unchanged and documented as unreachable pending a public WAN address; nothing shall be built that depends on it. THE ACCESS POLICY IS SERVER-SIDE AND SHALL NOT BE VERIFIED BY READING A LOCAL FILE. tailscaled never reads local disk for policy, so a check over a tracked artifact confirms only that this repo says what this repo says and is false-green when a wide-open policy is applied in the console beside an intact file. A tracked policy SHALL be carried as a reference to paste into the console, syntactically valid and free of rules targeting tags no device carries; it shall NOT be deployed to the hub, and no check shall report it as verification. Tailnet-lock state SHALL be queried and reported as a warning rather than a failure.
Rationale: Measured 2026-09-18: the WAN address is RFC1918 and an off-LAN request to the apex over cellular timed out, so the connection is behind carrier-grade NAT and no inbound path can be created from this side. An outbound-initiated tunnel is the only remote access that works without ISP cooperation. It is a host service because a subnet router must manage the host's routing table and forwarding sysctls, which is not a compose concern, and because it must be up before the stack is. Declining exit-node duty keeps household internet traffic off the hub. Declining the tunnel's DNS preserves split-horizon, which is the property that makes every service name resolve correctly on this LAN. The membership trust is the real cost and is stated rather than hidden: traffic is end-to-end encrypted and the coordinator cannot read it, but the coordinator decides which public keys are members, which is why node addition must be signature-gated and an ACL must exist before the second device joins.
AcceptanceCriteria: A test asserts the sysctl drop-in sets both forwarding keys and that the unit is enabled. A test asserts the daemon is absent from the compose file and present as a host unit, so the two lanes cannot drift. A test asserts LAN_CIDR admits the LAN and the tunnel range and excludes the docker bridge range. A test asserts no auth key literal appears in the repo, the payload or the materialised env. A test asserts the ACL artifact exists and is not allow-all. A test asserts the health check fails when authorised without tailnet lock, and fails on a multi-node tunnel with no ACL artifact, naming which control is absent. Hardware acceptance - a client on cellular reaching the hub AND one LAN-only host by address with no router forward, and confirmation that the source address Caddy records for a tunnel client is byte-identical to that client's assigned tunnel address, judged by reading Caddy's access log for a request known to have come over the tunnel - is named as open and is not claimed by any config-level check.
Permutations: install={apt,absent}; auth={interactive,unauthorised,expired}; routes={advertised-approved,advertised-unapproved,none}; client={cellular,lan,absent}; dns={technitium-preserved,tunnel-injected}; exitnode={declined,offered}; lan_cidr={both,lan-only,includes-bridge}

Title: Centralised LLM gateway distinct from the AI CLI lane
Requirement: The hub shall run one OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway as a profile-gated compose service, OFF by default, pinned by image digest and never by a floating tag. It shall hold provider credentials in an env file materialised by the existing secret tooling and shall require a bearer key of its own on every request, including from the LAN. It shall NOT publish a host port on the LAN address: it shall stay on the docker bridge and be reached through the existing Caddy, which already terminates TLS. Its Caddy host shall be gated by the same LAN_CIDR remote_ip rule SR-042 extends, so it answers the LAN and the tunnel and returns 403 to the internet before any handler runs. It shall be a SEPARATE SERVICE from ai-cli (SN-016/SR-019): ai-cli's bind to loopback or a docker bridge address shall not be relaxed, no route of ai-cli shall be exposed through this gateway, and the two shall not share a credential, an account or a volume. The gateway's README shall state its wider-reach departure explicitly, the way A40 stated ai-cli's. Consumers shall be configured with the gateway's URL and never a provider's, so a provider swap is invisible to them. The approved upstream shall be named in the spine together with its authoritative registry, and no other repository, namespace, mirror or fork shall be referenced; the pinned digest shall be verifiable against the publisher's signature rather than trusted as a copied hash, and a rotation shall re-verify and re-record the digest with its date and version in one reviewable commit. The approved upstream and its registry shall be named in the spine, and no fork, mirror or other namespace shall be referenced. The image shall be pinned BY DIGEST, recorded with its version and date, so that an upgrade is a reviewable commit. The upstream piped-shell installer shall NOT be used by any tracked script, unit or document: it is unpinned, executes remote code at deploy time, and yields a deployment no commit describes.
Rationale: Concentrating a dozen provider keys in one process is the point and also the risk, so the concentrator earns a bearer key, a digest pin and a stated departure rather than inheriting the stack's ambient LAN trust. Fronting with Caddy rather than binding the LAN address reuses a TLS terminator and an address gate that already exist and are already tested, instead of standing up a second exposure surface. The separation from ai-cli is not stylistic: ai-cli's posture — dedicated unprivileged account, pinned executable, read-only tool use, never the LAN — survived a cross-review that rejected the block with 16 findings, and the new lane's callers are deliberately wider. Folding them would silently widen the reviewed one. An earlier pass of this work REJECTED this upstream on provenance and selected a different one; that rejection was WRONG and is recorded here because the way it went wrong is the trap the next reader will meet. A search for the project returns FORKS RANKED ABOVE THE ORIGINAL - it has thousands - and the fork that was examined showed zero stars and pointed at what looked like an unrelated registry namespace. Both signals were artifacts of reading a fork: the counters were the fork's, and the namespace was the AUTHOR'S OWN. The canonical repository is named directly on the project's own site, which the Owner had linked from the outset and which was not consulted. The lesson carried forward into LLR-963 is to assume any result for this project is a fork until the author has been checked, and to treat the project site rather than a search ranking as the pointer of record. What survives from that pass and is NOT withdrawn: this service is a credential concentrator, so it earns a digest pin, its own bearer key and a stated bind departure; and upstream's own guidance that the project is local-first, single-user and should not be exposed publicly is consistent with reaching it only from the LAN and the tunnel.
AcceptanceCriteria: A test asserts the compose service is profile-gated and absent from the default profile. A test asserts the image reference is a digest and fails on a floating tag. A test asserts no host port publish exists for the service on the LAN address. A test asserts the gateway rejects an unauthenticated request and a wrong bearer key. A test asserts ai-cli's bind is unchanged and that no gateway route names an ai-cli endpoint. A test asserts the Caddy host carries the remote_ip gate with the 403 default rather than only an auth prompt. A model listing and a completion against a live provider are hardware/runtime acceptance and are named as open.
Permutations: profile={enabled,disabled}; image={digest,floating,absent}; auth={valid-bearer,absent,wrong}; caller={lan,tunnel,wan}; provider={reachable,429,5xx,timeout,all-down}; ai-cli={unchanged,bind-relaxed}; backend={free-tier,local-model,both}

Title: Dev-PC wake actuation and measured readiness state
Requirement: The hub shall run one profile-gated service that reports the dev PC's inference readiness as exactly one of off, waking, up, ready or failed, and that actuates a wake on request. THE DETERMINATION SHALL USE TWO SEPARATE LAYERS. Reachability - ICMP and a TCP connect to the inference port - decides off versus up, and a connect that times out or is refused with nothing else answering is off and SHALL NOT be reported as up. Readiness runs only on a host reachability already found up, and decides up versus ready: only a successful model listing that also names the target model as loaded is ready, while a listing that omits the model, errors or times out leaves the state at up. Precedence when the layers disagree shall be fixed: an expired wake deadline yields failed and outranks all probes, then reachability, then readiness. Only waking shall be estimated, it shall be entered solely by firing a wake, and it shall carry a bounded deadline after which it becomes failed - never waking indefinitely. A WAKE SHALL BE A SINGLE-FLIGHT OPERATION KEYED TO THE TARGET: concurrent requests shall join the in-flight wake rather than each starting one, the transition into waking shall be atomic, the flight shall own the deadline and joiners shall neither extend nor replace it, and a failed flight shall be cleared so a later request starts a new one. The state shall be served over HTTP for the gateway to consult, published to the existing broker, and exposed to the existing uptime monitor so a rotted wake path is discovered before a request discovers it. The wake mechanism shall be behind a named interface with the magic-packet implementation as one provider, because the dev PC's physical NIC is bound to a Hyper-V external vSwitch and the magic-packet path is UNPROVEN on that binding; a second provider shall be addable without touching the state machine. The gateway shall, on a request for a local model while the box is not ready, HOLD the request to a bounded cap while joining or starting the wake, and on expiry fall back to a configured non-local provider rather than returning an error. SLEEP POLICY AND SLEEP ACTUATION SHALL HAVE DIFFERENT OWNERS AND THE SPLIT SHALL BE EXPLICIT. The hub shall own POLICY: it shall publish a sleep-permission verdict (IF-026) that permits only when the configured idle period has elapsed with no local-model request AND the IF-025 session signal is a fresh, authenticated, detached reading, and shall fail closed to deny otherwise. The hub shall NOT actuate sleep and shall hold no credential capable of suspending the dev PC. The dev PC shall own ACTUATION: it shall POLL that verdict, opening no inbound endpoint of its own for this purpose, and shall re-check its own in-flight work immediately before suspending, declining a permitting verdict while work is running - which a remote command could not do, being evaluated when sent and applied when it arrives. The wake service shall perform NO blocking work while holding the lock that establishes its linearization point: wake actuation, reachability and readiness probing, broker publication and HTTP serving shall all occur after the lock is released, and waiters shall be notified from a list snapshotted under it, so that a waiter continuation cannot re-enter the lock and a slow network operation cannot stall every joiner and every state read. The sleep inhibit shall consume an explicit, authenticated session-attachment signal (IF-025) carrying its own observation instant, with a configured staleness bound, and shall FAIL CLOSED TO ATTACHED: an absent, stale, malformed or unauthenticated reading shall inhibit sleep exactly as an attached session does, because a false attached costs idle power until the next poll while a false detached suspends the machine mid-session.
Rationale: A woken machine answers ICMP tens of seconds before it can answer a prompt, so conflating up with ready produces caller timeouts that get blamed on the model. Callers — coding agents especially — tolerate a slow response far better than a 503, and free-tier fallback is always available because no local-only routing constraint was imposed. The wake path is the highest-risk unknown in this plan and the cheapest to disprove: Hyper-V external-switch binding has historically consumed the magic packet before the NIC's wake filter matches it, and the driver reports the filters armed either way, so the arming evidence is not evidence. Making the mechanism pluggable means a failed magic-packet test costs one provider, not the service. The sleep inhibit exists because an idle timer that fires while the Owner is working over the remote desktop makes the whole arrangement worse than leaving the box on.
AcceptanceCriteria: Tests assert each state's determining condition independently, that waking expires to failed at the deadline rather than persisting, and that a listing which returns 200 with the target model absent yields up and never ready. A test asserts the hold path returns a provider answer rather than an error when the cap expires, and that the wake fires once rather than per retry. A test asserts the idle timer does not fire while a session is attached. A test asserts the broker topic and the monitor probe both reflect a state transition. The magic-packet path through the vSwitch, from S3 and from S5, is HARDWARE acceptance, is named as open, and no config-level check may claim it.
Permutations: state={off,waking,up,ready,failed}; probe={icmp-only,tcp-only,both,neither}; listing={200-loaded,200-absent,500,timeout}; wake={magic-packet,alternate-provider,none}; sleepstate={s3,s5}; vswitch={bound,unbound}; deadline={within,expired}; hold={answers-in-cap,expires-to-fallback}; idle={no-session,session-attached}

Title: Self-hosted remote-desktop relay and service-mode client
Requirement: The hub shall run the self-hosted remote-desktop rendezvous and relay as two profile-gated compose services sharing ONE data volume, so both read the same key pair, with host networking for their documented TCP and UDP ports. BECAUSE THOSE ARE HOST SOCKETS AND NOT PUBLISHED CONTAINER PORTS, the LAN-and-tunnel-only restriction shall be enforced in the host INPUT chain for IPv4 and in the ip6tables INPUT chain for IPv6, and SHALL NOT be placed in DOCKER-USER, which such traffic never traverses; a DOCKER-USER rule here would be present, would appear to be a control, and would filter nothing. Both address families shall be covered, because a v4-only ruleset leaves the same listener reachable over v6. These ports shall NEVER be forwarded at the router. The generated public key shall be recorded as a deployment output and required of every client; a server reachable without it admits any caller who can reach it. The Windows client shall be installed AS A SERVICE from an administrator account, so it survives logout and can render the sign-in screen and elevation prompts, and its unattended password shall be a distinct high-entropy secret that is not the Owner's Windows password. The service's data volume shall join the local backup set, because the key pair is not reproducible from the repo. THE ISOLATION RULES SHALL BE DURABLE AND FAIL CLOSED. They shall be installed by a unit ordered before, and required by, the services whose sockets they protect, so that a failure to program either address family stops the listeners rather than exposing them; the installer shall be idempotent across a reboot, a firewall reload or a flush, removing its own prior rules by marker before installing the current set. Verification shall include a real connection attempt from a non-LAN, non-tunnel source to each documented TCP and UDP port after the firewall has been reloaded from a clean state, because a file that still contains the right rule says nothing about a netfilter table that was flushed. Both containers shall declare no restart policy, so the container runtime never starts them at boot, after a daemon restart or after a crash, and they shall be started only by a systemd unit that Requires= and is After= the isolation unit, so a fence failure stops the listeners existing rather than losing a race to them. A deliberate manual start by the Owner on their own machine is not defended against; the standing threat model does not justify carrying a mechanism for it.
Rationale: Service mode is the entire requirement, not a preference: a user-session process dies at logout and cannot draw the secure desktop, so a machine woken by SR-044 to a login screen would be unreachable exactly when remote access matters most. This is the same property SR-044's inference endpoint needs, and naming it once in both places is deliberate — getting it wrong makes wake, inference and remote desktop all half-work, and only after a cold wake. Host networking and one shared volume are the upstream-documented arrangement; two volumes silently produce two key pairs and a client that can reach the rendezvous but never the relay. The no-forward rule is what keeps this from becoming a new internet-facing exposure, and it is affordable only because SR-042 provides a remote path that needs no forward.
AcceptanceCriteria: A test asserts both services mount the same named volume and that the compose file declares it once. A test asserts the isolation rules land in INPUT and ip6tables INPUT, admit the LAN and tunnel CIDRs and reject others, and that a DOCKER-USER placement or a v4-only ruleset FAILS the check. A test asserts the volume appears in the local backup sources and not in the offsite set. A test asserts no router-forward instruction for these ports exists in any tracked config or doc. Client-side service-mode installation, reaching a genuinely LOGGED-OUT machine's sign-in screen, entering the credential, and then re-proving the whole path over the tunnel from cellular are HARDWARE acceptance and are named as open.
Permutations: volume={shared,split}; key={present,absent,rotated}; caller={lan,tunnel,wan}; session={logged-in,locked,logged-out,uac-prompt}; client={service-mode,user-session,portable}; port={tcp,udp,both}

Title: Continuity of the panel player sign-in across a reimage
Requirement: The wall image shall keep the panel music player's browser sign-in across an image reinstall, and shall not let its own rebuilds invalidate it. It shall provide a tool that saves the credential-bearing part of the player's browser profile to one archive and restores it into a freshly imaged panel, and firstboot shall restore a staged archive once. The restore shall refuse a profile a live browser holds, shall refuse to replace an existing sign-in unless told to, shall refuse an archive that does not carry one, and shall refuse any archive member outside the credential set. The cookie encryption backend shall be NAMED by the application rather than detected from the environment, and the client identity the player presents shall not carry the application or runtime version.
Rationale: MEASURED BEFORE BUILT, and the reported premise was wrong: no service reinstall loses this sign-in -- it survived every one of the ~67 paired releases between the 2026-09-11 reimage and 2026-09-18, with its session cookies re-issued on the 18th. A REIMAGE loses it, by recreating the panel account's home, and nothing carried it forward. Two other mechanisms can: the runtime's default client identity carries both the application and the runtime version and the dependency is a floating range, so a rebuild moves the fingerprint under a session the provider fronts with bot detection; and the browser SNIFFS its cookie-encryption backend from the desktop environment, so the day any package pulls a keyring onto the panel the backend flips and every cookie already on disk becomes undecryptable with nothing anywhere connecting the two. Naming the backend closes that and is also what makes an archive portable between boxes at all.
AcceptanceCriteria: A saved archive restores the sign-in onto an emptied profile. A save refuses when there is no sign-in to save and when a keyring is present, rather than writing an archive nobody can use. A restore refuses a held profile, refuses to overwrite an existing sign-in without an explicit flag, refuses an archive carrying no cookie store, and refuses an archive whole -- leaving the partition untouched -- when any member is a link, a device node, an escaping path or a file outside the credential set. A stale lock from a dead process does not block a restore. The derived client identity is unchanged by an application-version or runtime-patch bump, changes with a browser-engine major exactly as a browser update would, and is never invented from a runtime string that is not understood.
Permutations: archive={valid,no-cookies,storage-only,link,device-node,escaping,foreign-member,corrupt}; profile={empty,signed-in,held-by-a-live-browser,stale-lock}; keyring={absent,present}; replace={off,on}; identity={runtime-default,app-bump,runtime-patch,engine-major,unparseable}

Title: Two LLM lanes, one of which cannot reach a cloud provider
Requirement: The stack shall provide TWO OpenAI-compatible ingresses with different substitution behaviour, and the difference shall be enforced BELOW THE APPLICATION rather than by the application. THE PRIVATE LANE shall be a profile-gated proxy configured with EXACTLY ONE deployment - the dev PC's inference endpoint - holding no credential for any other provider, publishing no host port, carrying no reverse-proxy site, and running with its model store disabled so that its committed configuration file is authoritative and no deployment can be added at runtime that version control does not record. It shall declare no fallback of any kind. THE ABSENCE OF A CREDENTIAL SHALL NOT BE RELIED UPON AS THE BOUNDARY: the proxy registers provider pass-through routes independent of its deployment list and forwards caller-supplied credentials on them, so a credential can arrive in the request. The lane shall therefore take a STATIC address on a PINNED subnet, and a host firewall fence shall restrict it IN BOTH DIRECTIONS THAT EXIST. Forwarded egress shall permit only the dev PC's inference port plus established return traffic and reject the rest. HOST-DIRECTED TRAFFIC SHALL BE FENCED SEPARATELY AND IN A DIFFERENT CHAIN, because packets addressed to the host's own bridge address are delivered locally and the forwarded chain never sees them: only the bridge gateway on the readiness port shall be permitted, and all other host-directed traffic rejected. The host-directed rules shall be placed below the mesh-tunnel jump, which admits the tunnel at all, and above every blanket accept already present, and the fence shall verify that no accept precedes its reject rather than assuming a position. The lane shall declare no restart policy and shall be started only by a unit that requires the fence unit, so the container runtime can never start it unfenced; the fence shall be enabled unconditionally while the lane is enabled only on its own knob. An in-process route allowlist shall additionally remove the pass-through routes as defence in depth, and shall be documented as NOT the guarantee. THE PUBLIC LANE shall remain the existing gateway with its free-tier catalogue and quota metering, and shall reach the dev PC ONLY by directing its custom endpoint at the private lane, never at the dev PC directly, so that the wake-and-hold behaviour exists once and cannot be bypassed. THE HOLD SHALL LIVE IN THE PRIVATE LANE AND THE FALLBACK SHALL LIVE IN THE PUBLIC ONE: on a request for the local model while the dev PC is not ready, the private lane shall consult the readiness service, request at most one wake, hold while the readiness service is consulted, request at most one wake, and on expiry REFUSE with a response whose status and body the public lane classifies as retryable and which shall not resemble a rate-limit condition. EXACTLY ONE READINESS CHECK SHALL ALWAYS OCCUR, so that a zero cap asks once rather than refusing a box that is already ready, and every wait after that first check shall be inside the cap - the bound on total elapsed time is therefore the cap PLUS ONE PROBE TIMEOUT and shall be documented as such rather than as a hard cap. Both the readiness probe and the wake request shall be bounded by the remaining budget. Held-then-fell-back is therefore a property of the system and of NO SINGLE COMPONENT. Timing parameters shall be validated at startup, rejecting non-finite and non-positive values, because a non-finite cap makes every expiry comparison false and the hold would hang rather than fail. Where the readiness service is not configured the hold shall be disabled explicitly and announced at startup.
Rationale: SR-044's hold was specified when one component was going to both hold and fall back. Two consumers want opposite things from the same event: a finance audit must ERROR rather than have a cloud provider answer with snapshot-derived data, while a coding agent wants an answer from somewhere. The gateway cannot express both - measured on the running container, its fallback chain is selected with no user, key or caller column, a named model is moved to the front of that chain rather than pinned, and connection-refused and timeout are both on its retryable list, which are exactly the states of a machine that sleeps by design. THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS REQUIREMENT SAID THE PRIVATE LANE'S GUARANTEE FOLLOWED FROM HOLDING NO CREDENTIAL. An adversarial review disproved it: the proxy ships thirty-two provider pass-through routes registered independently of the deployment list, its Vertex handler forwards caller-supplied credentials when it holds none of its own, and a probe request carrying such a header opened a connection to a Google endpoint. A property that depends on the caller not supplying a credential is not a property. The rejected alternative - one proxy holding every credential with a per-key model allowlist - fails for the same reason one level up: it is a check inside a process that still has the credentials. Content-based routing was also rejected: its detection is regex and keyword, so an ordinary merchant line carrying a name and an amount matches nothing and fails OPEN. Sensitivity is therefore expressed by which process a caller can reach AND by what that process is permitted to send.
AcceptanceCriteria: Tests assert against the artifacts actually loaded, as WHITELISTS rather than blacklists of provider names: exactly one deployment; its endpoint is the one permitted environment reference; no literal URL anywhere in the live configuration; no fallback key at any depth; the model store disabled; an exact declared placeholder in the credential slot; exactly the two read-only configuration mounts and no named volume; no host port and no reverse-proxy site; the image pinned by digest matching both the pin file and the example environment. The fence is asserted for BOTH chains, rule content, refusal of empty and hostname values, read-back, RULE ORDER, and that no accept precedes its reject, and the lane for restart:no, a unit that requires the fence, a fence ordered before the container runtime, and absence from the default profile list. The route allowlist is asserted to exclude every provider pass-through prefix and the configuration to state that it is not the guarantee. The refusal is asserted against the PUBLIC lane's own vendored retryability matcher rather than against the file the message is defined in, and separately VERIFIED ON THE WIRE against the running container, which returns HTTP 503 with the message intact. Title: Call bridge through the panel
Requirement: The wall image shall observe when a gateway it is the hands-free unit for has a voice link up, and shall publish that as a call. Where the headset position additionally resolves to a Bluetooth headset, the image shall bridge the call to it: the gateway's far end onto the merged bus, the merged bus to the headset, the headset's own microphone as the selected microphone, and that selected microphone back to the gateway. While bridging, the image shall not also run the headset's music-profile leg, and shall restore it when the bridge ends only if the switch still asks for it. The input mute shall stop both microphone directions and shall not silence the far end. The call shall be published as an observation and never offered as a command, since the gateway places it and the gateway ends it; it shall carry aliases only, shall remain readable for as long as it lasts, and every failure to observe, to form or to publish shall answer 'no call' rather than a partly asserted bridge. The panel shall show that it is on a call, and shall show separately that the call is being passed through to a headset.
Rationale: Owner ruling 2026-09-19: 'build the bridge, and show it' -- 'Connected to a call' is presented, and an icon next to the output selector says the passthrough bridge is active. The bridge is the only arrangement in which the panel's own mute and echo canceller sit inside somebody's call, which is both its value and its risk, and it is the only one in which the panel can say 'I am on a call' at all. TWO SIMULTANEOUS VOICE LINKS WERE MEASURED ON THIS ADAPTER on 2026-09-19, which is what withdrew the earlier hardware objection: the panel held one as hands-free unit to a desktop and one to a phone at the same time. THE MUSIC LEG MUST GO DOWN because the music and voice profiles are exclusive on one peer, so while bridging the headset hears the whole merged bus at narrowband mono; that is the profile and not a defect, and it is why the bridge exists only for the duration of a call. IT IS HELD DOWN BY A MARKER FILE AND NOT BY A MATCH AGAINST THE PUBLISHED STATE, because a unit condition cannot carry a quoted fragment of that document through both systemd's parser and the shell's without one of them eating a quote, and a condition that silently matched nothing would start the music leg under a live voice link with nothing in the journal to connect the two. Two defects of 2026-09-19 are recorded here because both were invisible from the code that caused them: the supervisor restarted the music leg whenever a call ended, and 'the call ended' says nothing about where the switch is, so a call ending in the Speaker position played the room into the headset; and the published call was written only when the fact changed while its reader ages it off the file's timestamp, so a call doing what calls mostly do -- continuing -- was reported as no call within half a minute with every leg still running. THE ECHO CANCELLER'S SEAM IS UNCHANGED: in the Speaker position on a call the far end is room output like any other and is removed from the microphone before it goes back up the link, and in the bridge the headset's microphone does not hear the room at all.
AcceptanceCriteria: Supervisor tests assert the three states and their boundary: a gateway voice link with the position resolving anywhere but Bluetooth is a call, the same link with it resolving to Bluetooth is a bridge, and no link is no call. They assert the four legs address what they claim -- the bus to the headset and the headset's microphone into the loopback, not the reverse, since swapped the Owner would hear themselves -- that the headset's capture is opened at the rate the link negotiated because the conversion plugin cannot wrap a capture, and that the gateway-role objects are matched by a pattern that does not also match the hands-free-role ones. They assert the mute stops both microphone directions and leaves the far end audible, that the music leg is gated on the published resolution rather than on a headset address that is present whenever a headset is, that the marker is written before the music leg is stopped and removed before it is started, and that a call which merely continues stays readable past the staleness bound. Boundary tests assert the published call carries aliases only, that an address-shaped one is refused at the broker, at the host and at the renderer independently, that a headset is named only while actually bridged, and that a missing or damaged document is 'no call' and never an error.
Permutations: call={absent,up,lost}; resolution={bluetooth,usb,none}; state={idle,call,bridge}; mute={on,off,arrives-mid-bridge}; marker={present,absent}; ag-link={present,absent,rate-unreadable}; far-end-knob={on,off}; document={fresh,stale,missing,damaged,alias-invalid}; end={hangup,headset-off,supervisor-restart}

Title: Hub recovery evidence and boot accounting, always on
Requirement: The hub shall record, whether or not recovery is enabled, the evidence a later recovery decision or root-cause analysis needs, and shall count every reboot by how it ended. Every 30 s it shall log one record of memory pressure (PSI), available memory and free swap, every container's memory, every protected container and protected host service IN FULL, the five largest host processes and the tasks in uninterruptible sleep, read from procfs, cgroupfs and Docker's own metadata files and never from the Docker daemon. Late in every shutdown, after Docker has stopped and before filesystems are unmounted, it shall write a clean-shutdown stamp carrying the boot id, UTC and any recovery intent left in tmpfs, durably (temp file, fsync, rename, directory fsync). Early in every boot it shall classify the previous boot as clean, recovery, watchdog, panic or unexplained, bound to the previous boot's id, and commit that durably; if the commit fails, recovery shall run report-only for that boot. The journal shall be persistent with a pinned size cap and every hung task reported. The library backup shall run in its own slice whose memory peak is logged after every run, with an opt-in memory limit whose swap limit is equal and whose default is no limit; a run that finds staging left by an interrupted run shall refuse with a line naming the recovery event that interrupted it.
Rationale: The 2026-10-04 wedge left no pressure record, no account of how the box ended, and a backup peak that 10 s polling could only bound from below. Thresholds cannot be calibrated, nor a loop braked, from evidence that does not exist; so evidence is P1 and always on (Owner D1), and nothing in this requirement acts on anything. Boot-id binding and atomic commits answer R2-2: an intent lost to a slow disk, or a commit lost to a reset, must not turn a recovery into a clean boot. The slice's peak is the peak since boot across runs, an UPPER bound for any one run, which is the direction a limit must be sized from (R2-8).
AcceptanceCriteria: Hermetic tests drive the classifier against a temporary root for all five classes, a stamp naming another boot, a CARDRESET overriding a stamp, an old pstore record, and the capability's first boot; assert that a commit writes boots.log, rebinds last-boot and deletes the stamp, that a second run in the same boot appends nothing, that a failed fsync leaves the committed file and no temp file behind and that a directory fsync follows every rename, and that a commit failure makes the supervisor report-only. The sampler is asserted on a fake tree to log a small protected container, a protected host unit's cgroup memory and RSS, the top five and the D-state tasks. The wrapper is executed to log the slice peak after backup and verify, to survive an unreadable slice, and to refuse on a left-behind Temp naming the event that names the backup while leaving Temp untouched. validate_config asserts every unit is installed and every host knob declared. Stamp ordering in a real shutdown, journald's cap and the slice's survival across --rm containers are lab cases (L-3, L-13) and are NOT proven here.
Permutations: previous={clean,recovery,watchdog,panic,unexplained,first}; stamp={absent,this-boot,other-boot,with-intent}; bootstatus={absent,0,CARDRESET}; pstore={none,new,seen}; commit={ok,ENOSPC}; slice={readable,absent}; staging={clean,left-behind}; event={names-backup,unrelated,older-than-temp,none}

Title: Hub recovery supervisor: measured early kill, quarantine and sshd restart
Requirement: When HUB_WATCHDOG_ENABLED is true the hub shall run one supervisor, standard library only, that samples memory PSI full avg10 every 5 s on CLOCK_MONOTONIC and kills the largest eligible container through cgroup.kill when an episode has lasted HUB_WD_KILL_SECONDS (120) and at least HUB_WD_KILL_MEASURED_PCT (75) of the window's MEASURED samples were at or above HUB_WD_PSI_FULL (40), at most three kills per rolling hour with a 60 s cooldown. Scheduling gaps shall be recorded and never counted as measured pressure; a suspend (BOOTTIME minus MONOTONIC growing by more than 5 s) shall reset the state. Victims shall be container scopes only, never host processes; containers in HUB_WD_PROTECT, under 256 MiB, or not identifiable from Docker's metadata shall be skipped, and a protected container that is the largest shall be recorded as would-have-killed. A kill shall be confirmed by cgroup.events populated 0 within 10 s and reconciled with Docker asynchronously and boundedly, removing or restarting a container Docker still reports running. A compose service killed twice within an hour shall on the next selection be quarantined (restart policy no, stopped, survives a reboot) without spending kill budget, until released. sshd shall be restarted after HUB_WD_SSH_FAILS banner-probe failures 60 s apart while memory is normal. The main thread shall never block on a disk, journald or D-Bus; actions shall run on one action thread from non-droppable, deduplicated per-kind queues; telemetry shall run on two daemon threads from a bounded drop-oldest queue. The supervisor shall run OOM-immune, at the lowest realtime priority with a realtime CPU limit, memory-locked within a finite cap, and shall run report-only whenever setup fails or the boot was not accounted. earlyoom shall be configured as a fast-spike backstop from HUB_OOM_* and tailscaled protected from OOM selection; the image shall ship earlyoom disabled, so it never runs before the knob has been converged on.
Rationale: The 10-04 thrash was a container outgrowing the box while nothing that could act was scheduled. Killing on measured pressure only, never on gaps, answers R2-9; cgroup.kill needs no daemon, and confirmation plus reconciliation answer R2-5's ghost. Quarantine stops one restart-policy workload spending the whole budget. The thread split answers R2-3: Python cannot cancel a thread blocked in fsync, so nothing that matters may wait on telemetry. sshd receives no unit-level OOM drop-in: OpenSSH already runs its listener at -1000 and restores each session to the inherited value (measured on the hub), so a -1000 unit setting would make every SSH session unkillable.
AcceptanceCriteria: Hermetic tests with injected clocks, procfs, cgroupfs, device, probe and runner assert: one kill at 120 s and none in cooldown; a single gap, unreadable PSI and sparse samples never kill; 67 % pressured never kills; a kill does not reset t0; a wall-clock jump changes nothing; a suspend resets; protected, small and unidentified containers are skipped, the backup slice is scanned, host cgroups are never candidates; a second kill of one service within the hour quarantines without spending budget and is executed as update plus stop; populated 0 confirms, a kill that does not take is recorded, a ghost is removed or restarted by restart policy, an unanswered Docker is retried and never waited on; telemetry blocked for ever does not stop an sshd restart or petting; workers drop to SCHED_OTHER and a worker that cannot is a setup failure; unaccounted boots act on nothing. 30 mutations each turn a targeted test red. Behaviour under a real thrash, real realtime scheduling, mlockall on the hub and earlyoom's choice are lab cases L-1, L-2, L-2b, L-6, L-8, L-EO, L-10 and are NOT proven here.
Permutations: psi={calm,pressured,unreadable}; cadence={5s,gap}; clock={steady,wall-jump,suspend}; victim={eligible,protected,small,unidentified,host,backup-slice}; kill={confirmed,did-not-take}; docker={agrees,ghost-restart,ghost-rm,no-answer}; repeat={first,second-in-hour}; telemetry={flowing,blocked}; mode={contain,braked,report-only}; sshd={answers,silent}

Title: Hub reset device, shutdown hand-off and loop brake
Requirement: With HUB_WD_TIERS=full the supervisor shall request a graceful reboot when an episode is still open HUB_WD_REBOOT_SECONDS (600) after it began, writing its intent to tmpfs first, and shall drive a hardware watchdog chosen in the order wdat_wdt, iTCO_wdt, softdog, none, persisted for later boots, at HUB_WD_HW_TIMEOUT (60). It shall stop petting if no SIGTERM arrives within 120 s of the reboot request, on a MemoryError in its main loop, or by dying, and shall not be restarted automatically. On SIGTERM it shall raise the device timeout to HUB_WD_SHUTDOWN_SECONDS (300), pet once and exit WITHOUT the magic close, and systemd's RebootWatchdogSec shall cover the late shutdown with the same bound on the same device. It shall magic-close only on an explicit disarm that names the current boot and the running invocation, which is consumed when read, and a disarm shall count only when the device is then verified inactive - otherwise the device is kept and petted and nothing is stopped; every setup-controlled replacement of a running supervisor shall go through that disarm, and timeouts shall be validated against the device's own range before it is opened; the unit shall have no ExecStop. Three counted boots in 24 h shall engage a brake that sets kernel.panic=0, opens no device and never reboots while kills, sshd restarts and quarantine continue; it shall clear only after 24 h without a counted boot or on an explicit reset. Recovery, watchdog and panic boots shall always count; unexplained boots shall count until the selected reset device has once reported WDIOF_CARDRESET, after which they shall not while a device with that identity remains selected. Turning the knob off shall disarm before anything stops the supervisor, refuse to stop one it cannot disarm, remove every drop-in and restore kernel.panic=0.
Rationale: R2-1: ExecStop runs on every stop including a reboot's, so a disarm placed there disarms every recovery reboot. R2-4: systemd-shutdown reopens the device in late shutdown whatever RuntimeWatchdogSec says, so the hand-off is made explicit. R2-2: a panic reboot is a loop the brake must also gate, hence kernel.panic. D10: a power cut and a watchdog reset are indistinguishable unless the firmware reports CARDRESET, so the counting policy follows what the board has demonstrated rather than a configured belief. Worst case from t0 to a reset is about 22 minutes, a bound and not a prediction.
AcceptanceCriteria: Hermetic tests assert: SIGTERM without authorisation sets 300, pets, closes, no magic close and exits through the injected exit; matching boot and invocation magic-closes and consumes the file; stale, foreign, empty and garbage authorisations are ignored and consumed; the unit has no ExecStop and carries the envelope; a reboot request is queued once, never re-queued after failure and its intent names the boot; a hung systemctl reboot still stops petting at 120 s; the third counted boot brakes, sets kernel.panic 0 and opens no device; panic is 10 only when enabled, full, committed and unbraked; the brake holds until 24 h after the LAST counted boot and a reset discards history; D10 counts unexplained boots until a CARDRESET latches proof; setup chooses wdat_wdt then iTCO_wdt then softdog, installs RebootWatchdogSec and re-executes PID 1 only on change, and the off path disarms before disable and refuses to stop an undisarmable supervisor. Whether this board resets on expiry, whether WDAT reports CARDRESET, and both shutdown-phase stalls are the P4 on-hub test and lab L-3 to L-7b, L-11, L-12, and are NOT proven here.
Permutations: tiers={contain,full}; device={wdat_wdt,iTCO_wdt,softdog,none}; sigterm={reboot,restart,disarm,stale-disarm}; escalation={sigterm-in-time,none-in-120s}; counted={0,2,3,4-after-23h}; reset={none,explicit,24h-quiet}; bootstatus={unproven,proven}; knob-off={idle,armed,undisarmable}

Title: AI-usage feeder: a dead login goes grey and stays grey
Requirement: A failure the feeder CLASSIFIES AS AUTHENTICATION shall grey the source's gauges once it is CONFIRMED - by failed authentication ATTEMPTS numbering at least two (AUTH_CONFIRM_ATTEMPTS) and spanning at least ten minutes from the first to the latest (AUTH_CONFIRM_SECONDS) - and they shall stay grey until a real reading arrives. Only attempts count: a cycle that skips the source (SR-095) adds neither an attempt nor any span. A success resets the history; a failure of any other kind leaves it unchanged. Authentication means: an HTTP 401; Codex's token_expired; Claude's credential file carrying no usable key (Claude readers only); Gemini's access token past its own expiry_date. The failure shall be a typed AuthFailure(SourceFailure) that reaches the per-source loop unwrapped. The history shall live in the state file in the source's schedule entry, under one reserved key with its own validator; on confirmation each stored reading of the source shall be replaced by an auth marker (key kept, own validator) so that a later failure of any other kind cannot restore the old colour and an optional gauge still posts. Every other failure keeps today's behaviour.
Rationale: A failed source used to re-post its last real value at its original observed_at, so a dead login kept its number in colour until NagLight's horizon passed: Codex was rejected for six days and Claude for a day on 2026-10-11 and the wall looked healthy. The rule was first 'two consecutive cycles', written for a 10-minute timer; with the timer at one minute (SR-096, Owner 2026-10-22) that would grey a gauge two minutes into a blip, so it is stated in attempts over time. Ten minutes absorbs the Claude refresh unit rewriting the credential mid-read and an access token that lapses minutes before its renewal (measured on the hub 2026-10-12..21: 14 Claude 401s, each cleared by the next refresher run). A network failure says nothing about the login, so it neither resets nor advances the history. Both feeders are one-shot units, so only the state file can carry the history, and the state loader drops anything it cannot validate. The key must be kept: state_keys decides whether an optional gauge (the Fable band) is posted at all.
AcceptanceCriteria: Failed attempts inside ten minutes, however many, re-post the last reading; attempts spanning ten minutes post no observed_at and mark the stored entry; two attempts ten minutes apart are enough; the history survives save/load and a fresh process; a success resets it and a non-auth failure leaves it; skipped cycles between attempts add no attempt and no span; confirmed then network stays stale on arrival; the Fable gauge still posts, stale, after confirmation and after a following network failure; a gauge never posted is not conjured; the same words from the OpenCode reader are not authentication; no reader re-wraps an AuthFailure; a state file holding the old counter loads with every reading and marker intact.
Permutations: failure={401;token_expired;no-usable-key;expired-token;network;5xx}; attempts={1;2;11}; span={<600s;>=600s}; between={skip;network;success}; gauge={required;optional}; history={none;reading;marker}
