Requirement: The feeder shall key each myAir record by its NIGHT KEY, the local calendar date on which the night ended, which is `startDate` + 1 calendar day (S0b, 2026-10-11, confirmed in the app), in the zone named by the TIMEZONE knob, which it refuses to guess. It shall keep ONE entry per night key, upserted. It shall publish only a finite `sleepScore` within 0..100 INCLUDING myAir's own 0, and shall treat a null, missing, non-numeric, boolean, NaN, infinite or out-of-range score as NO DATA and never as 0. A new night's observed_at shall be the EARLIER of 12:00 local on the night-key date and the time of first publication, and shall be FROZEN: a later correction changes the value and never observed_at, and a later fetch time is never used. The expected night is today's local date. Before 14:00 local with no record for it, the previous night's score shall stay and age normally - but only if the feeder PUBLISHED that night, a separate persisted set - and nothing older shall be shown; from 14:00 local with no record for it - which includes a newest record that is not for the expected night - the feeder shall post the unavailable body. All times shall be derived from the zone's offset at the instant concerned, never by adding hours, so the 23- and 25-hour days are right. The clock shall be re-read after the fetch before selecting and posting, and a local date earlier than the newest published night shall refuse to fetch, select or publish. The host clock shall be verified synchronised (systemd-timesyncd's flag file, else timedatectl NTPSynchronized, else unknown = not synchronised) before myAir is asked or any timestamped score is published; when it is not (or cannot be shown to be), the feeder shall still post the unavailable body, which carries no observed_at and needs no trusted time, on every such tick. The expected night shall never be first published before 06:00 local (it is staged, its frozen stamp floored at 06:00); once today's night has been published no earlier night shall be selected for display that day; an observation stamped in the future shall be quarantined, never destroyed; and a published key later than tomorrow shall be dropped on load.
Rationale: Cloud lag must never paint a false zero, an old night must never be shown as last night, and a stamp in the future reads as STALE in NagLight, so a score arriving at 07:00 stamped 12:00 would show grey until noon. There is no per-record upload time in myAir's nightly query, so first publication is the only honest clock; freezing it is what stops a revised night looking fresh. Whether an unused night comes back as a record or as no record at all is UNPROVEN (S0b), so both are made right.
AcceptanceCriteria: Absent record, null score, zero score, late upload, correction, 07:00 and 13:00 arrivals, 13:59 versus 14:00, both DST change days, a newest record two nights old, conflicting duplicates, a record whose night key is tomorrow, restart, a corrupt state file; each time-dependent case under a hand-written zone and under zoneinfo where present.
Permutations: score={absent,null,string,bool,NaN,inf,-1,0,82,100,101}; arrival={07:00,13:00,16:45}; clock={13:59,14:00}; day={ordinary,spring-forward,fall-back}

Title: Sleep feeder: standard-library myAir sign-in, and a dead login goes grey and stays grey
Requirement: The feeder shall sign in to myAir (NA) using the Python standard library only and the flow S0b observed - Okta authn, an authorization code with PKCE S256 read from the redirect Location fragment (the redirect never followed), the token endpoint, then one AppSync GraphQL query of the last 30 days asking only for startDate and sleepScore - from scratch every cycle, holding no refresh token and writing no session or token file. MYAIR_EMAIL and MYAIR_PASSWORD shall come from the environment, MYAIR_PASSWORD with the materialiser's doubled dollar collapsed, and neither shall ever be logged, echoed, persisted or put in an exception. A failure CLASSIFIED AS AUTHENTICATION shall be a typed AuthFailure: an Okta HTTP 401, an authn status other than SUCCESS (wrong password, locked, expired, MFA_REQUIRED), or a GraphQL 401 or unauthorized after a good sign-in. It shall be confirmed over two consecutive cycles by a count in the state file under a reserved key with its own validator, and on confirmation the gauge shall post the unavailable body and STAY unavailable, through any later failure of any kind, until a sign-in succeeds. Every other failure keeps the last score on its horizon. myAir shall be asked only inside fetch windows (about five sign-ins a day while the timer ticks every 30 minutes and every tick posts from stored state), and not at all for 6 h after a confirmed failure (24 h for LOCKED_OUT) except on --retry-now, and then only between 06:00 and 22:00 local. A fetch slot shall be marked done only after a read that did not fail, and a failed read may be retried at most twice more, 30 minutes apart, none from 22:00. --retry-now shall refuse to run as root or on a state file owned by another user. MFA_REQUIRED shall log that myAir now asks for an emailed code and a person must sign in, and the feeder shall contain no code that reads any mailbox.
Rationale: Plan 3.6 (G2): a dead login kept its last number in colour for days on the other feeders before this rule. Okta gives no refresh token for this client, so the only honest design is a fresh sign-in each cycle and a grey gauge when it is refused. The two-cycle confirmation absorbs a credential being rotated mid-read, and only the state file can carry the count because the unit is one-shot. A remote's own words (an Okta summary, a GraphQL message) can reflect a request back, so none is reproduced; only allow-listed status words are. The Owner ruled there is no automated reading of the household's email, ever.
AcceptanceCriteria: The loopback Okta checks the PKCE verifier against the challenge, the cookie the first call hands out, the session token and the bearer token; 401, LOCKED_OUT, MFA_REQUIRED, GraphQL unauthorized are auth and 500, 429, 403, timeout, dead port and a malformed body are not; one auth failure keeps the score, two grey it, auth-auth-network stays grey, a success clears it; the count survives a restart and a non-auth outcome resets it; the code imports no mail library.
Permutations: failure={401,LOCKED_OUT,PASSWORD_EXPIRED,MFA_REQUIRED,unauthorized,500,429,timeout,dead-port,malformed}; sequence={A,AA,AAN,ANA,AAS}

Title: Weight feeder: a daily resting heart rate gauge from the same Google Health connection (opt-in)
Requirement: The hub shall, when HEART_ENABLED is a literal 1 or true (default 0) and the weight feeder is itself enabled, post one gauge under the id `heart` to NagLight's POST /api/feed: label `Heart`, icon `heart`, unit `bpm`, the day's resting heart rate as `value`, explicit `min`/`max`/`target` taken from HEART_MIN_BPM (40), HEART_MAX_BPM (100) and HEART_TARGET_BPM (60), `favourable: low`, `window: {kind: daily}` with no start, end or direction, and an `observed_at` that is the data point's own civil date stamped at a fixed 12:00 LOCAL in the hub's TIMEZONE (inside NagLight's 02:00-local tracking day for that date) and never the fetch time; shall REFUSE to run the heart gauge, with a status line and weight untouched, when TIMEZONE is unset or unknown, never guessing UTC; shall read it from the SAME Google Health v4 route and refresh token as weight, data type `daily-resting-heart-rate`, under the SAME scope, so that no new consent is asked; shall refuse (never clamp) a reading outside 25..200 bpm and any `beatsPerMinute` that is not the plain decimal int64 string; shall post the stale-on-arrival body (value 0, no `observed_at`) when Google has no resting heart rate, without a failure line, and never invent a value; shall count sign-in failures for the heart source separately from weight's and grey on the second consecutive one exactly as weight does; and shall be a separate cycle that can neither change what the weight gauge posts nor be stopped by it. AMENDED 2026-10-25 (the Owner's ruling, HomeHub docs/HEART_GAUGE_PLAN_2026-10-25.md): with HEART_SOURCE=samples the value shall instead be a nightly resting heart rate the hub computes from Google Health's 5-minute heart-rate samples - the lowest mean of 6 consecutive samples inside the night's window after blips are dropped - and the target shall be the median of up to 28 earlier valid nights from the same device once 7 exist (HEART_TARGET_BPM, 75, until then), with min and max centred on it (HEART_COLOUR_SPAN_BPM, 24), published under the sleep gauge's nightly contract (06:00 floor, frozen stamp, 14:00 rule); see LLR-1314..LLR-1319. AMENDED 2026-10-25 (later): a long-term goal row in the Sheet (target bpm and due date) glides the target from the usual to the goal, the target being the lower of the two; see LLR-1320.
Rationale: The Owner's direction of 2026-10-11 is a wall heart-health gauge measuring daily resting heart rate, built NOW so a Fitbit-family device writing to Google Health later lights it up with no new code and no new consent. The data-types table lists daily-resting-heart-rate under the same health_metrics_and_measurements.readonly scope as weight and height; the discovery document (revision 20261007) names the member dailyRestingHeartRate with beatsPerMinute (an int64 string) and a civil date and NO instant, which is why the stamp is the date and never the clock. A resting rate outside the band is a units error or corruption, and a clamped number would be one nobody measured. The two sources share one credential but each makes its own refresh and keeps its own count, because a shared counter would be bumped twice per cycle and confirm a dead login after one. The heart half is its own cycle so a heart fault or a bad heart knob cannot touch the weight gauge, which is the promise this feeder was built around.
AcceptanceCriteria: With HEART_ENABLED unset, 0, false, yes or True nothing is fetched, posted or written and no socket is opened. With it on and a schema-shaped page the posted body is exactly {kind,id,label,icon,unit,value,min,max,target,favourable,window,observed_at}, passes NagLight's own Validate, is fresh for 36 h from the date stamp, and the real NagLight code agrees. An empty history posts value 0 with no observed_at and no failure line and writes nothing. A bare number, float, signed, padded or non-ASCII beatsPerMinute, an out-of-band rate, a malformed or partial date and a disagreeing pair for the newest day are refused with no value in the journal; a plausible rate outside the bar (38, 104) is posted as measured. One dead token leaves both counts at 1 after the first cycle and greys both on the second, and a following network failure stays grey. Whatever the heart reader does, the weight body and the weight keys of the state file are byte-identical to a run without it, and a missing weight goal or a bad heart knob does not stop the other half.
Permutations: enabled={unset,0,1,true,false,yes,True}; knobs={default,valid,non-numeric,negative,fractional,above 300,min>=max,target outside}; data={present,empty,null list,absent key,future day,far-future day,pre-feeder day,other data type,tie agreeing,tie disagreeing}; bpm={string,number,float,signed,padded,leading zero,non-ASCII,out of band,edge 25 and 200,outside bar}; auth={none,1,2,3 then network,network between,restart,renewed}; isolation={heart ok,no data,auth,network,bug,implausible} x {weight ok,auth,network,goal missing}; samples mode: TC-1486..TC-1493

Title: Sleep feeder: first boot installs it when the hub's .env says SLEEP_ENABLED=true, and the image payload carries it
Requirement: The hub's first-boot script shall, when and only when the .env value SLEEP_ENABLED is the literal `true` (quotes and a trailing carriage return ignored; `True`, `1`, `yes`, blank and absent all mean off), run stack/sleep/setup-sleep.sh from the deployed tree, after the weight feeder's block and before hub recovery. A refusal or failure of that script (a blank SLEEP_USER, SLEEP_FEED_URL, MYAIR_EMAIL or MYAIR_PASSWORD exits 2) shall be logged as a WARNING that names the reason and the re-run command and shall never fail the first boot. An enabled box whose payload lacks the script shall log that carriage is missing. The image payload shall be the committed repository tree, so that stack/sleep/ is carried without being named in any list.
Rationale: A feeder that was built, tested and merged but is called by nothing never runs: the weight feeder's block is the precedent, and the panel lane once shipped a payload missing a whole tree and went green.
AcceptanceCriteria: A first-boot block extracted from firstboot.sh and run against a stub setup script calls it for SLEEP_ENABLED=true (also quoted, also with CRLF) and for nothing else; a stub that exits 2 produces the WARNING and a zero exit under set -euo pipefail; a missing script produces the carriage-missing line; all six files under stack/sleep/ are tracked; the payload builder archives HEAD and the late-command copies the payload tree whole.
Permutations: SLEEP_ENABLED={true,"true",true+CR,false,blank,absent,True,1,yes}; setup={ok,refuses,missing}

Title: Sleep and heart knobs: one set of names from the deploy tooling to the hub, sleep on and heart off, and the running-hub install written down
Requirement: Every SLEEP_* and MYAIR_* name the sleep feeder reads, and every HEART_* name the heart reader reads, shall be declared in the deploy tooling's field schema and carried in stack/.env.example with exactly one line each, at the defaults SLEEP_ENABLED=false, SLEEP_USER blank, HEART_ENABLED=0 and the documented bounds, so that the materialiser emits them rather than skipping them. The hub's deploy configuration shall turn the sleep feeder on and name its identity from the identity table (never a literal value in a tracked file), and shall leave the heart gauge off. The heart gauge shall need no first-boot hook of its own: it shall reach the feeder through the weight unit's EnvironmentFile=. The sleep README shall give the in-place install procedure for a running hub whose /opt/homehub is not a git checkout: back the .env up, add only the missing lines in place, diff and copy only the sleep tree, run the setup script, and verify by timer, journal and a posted gauge.
Rationale: The deploy pipeline and the feeder were written by different sessions; a name present on one side only is a knob that silently does nothing, and the running hub is changed by hand, so the hand has to have a procedure.
AcceptanceCriteria: A test reads every environment name out of the feeder sources and finds each declared in the schema and present once in the template; the hub configuration holds the token and not a value; the weight unit takes the whole .env and the weight setup script neither filters it nor reads HEART_*; the README procedure is present and the stale 'firstboot does not yet call it' claim is gone.
Permutations: n/a

Title: AI CLI provisioning: the hub installs exactly the CLIs its enabled consumers need, from pinned, checksum-verified vendor artifacts
Requirement: A provisioner (stack/ai-cli/provision-ai-clis.sh) shall install, online and without operator action, exactly the AI CLIs that the enabled consumers need: the AI-usage feeder's AI_USAGE_SOURCES entries when AI_USAGE_ENABLED is true, and, when AI_CLI_ENABLED is true, the CLI the ai-cli service runs plus Codex only when an enabled ai-cli route belongs to the OPENAI family (classified against the registry and enable-list the service itself resolves, AI_CLI_REGISTRY and AI_CLI_ENABLED_ROUTES). Every artifact shall be named by a committed manifest row (version, https URL, sha256, size, archive kind, whole-tree inventory, entry point, version command, target platform, dependency), verified against that sha256 and size before anything is extracted, and installed under a root-owned prefix in a directory named by an install identity that includes the pinned version, the artifact hash, the wrapper revision and any dependency pin. The private Node runtime that Gemini needs shall live in that prefix, be referenced only by the Gemini wrapper by absolute path, and never be linked into /usr/local/bin. Nothing the operator has to read shall describe a CLI as a missing package: the output states what was installed, what is still owed and when it will be retried, and logins remain a human step.
Rationale: SN-016 said the CLIs are installed by hand over SSH outside the offline closure, so a deploy that enabled a source whose CLI was absent produced an error code about a package. The Owner ruled on 2026-10-11 that the deployers always package or pull what a configuration needs and that only logins stay human. Online, pinned and checksummed is the smaller design than an offline bundle and leaves no build-side artifact to keep honest; the offline bundle is parked. The hash is trust-on-first-pin, so the manifest is the reviewed place where a version changes.
AcceptanceCriteria: With the shipped manifest every row parses, its version equals the version token in its URL and matches its version regex, no URL is http, every source named is a reader the feeder has, and the Codex and Gemini inventories are whole-tree. Against local archive fixtures the enabled set is installed and nothing else; a checksum, size, version or inventory mismatch installs nothing; a changed Node pin or wrapper revision yields a new identity and a reinstall and an untrusted directory at an identity path is replaced, never reused; hostile archives (absolute, dot-dot, escaping symlink or hardlink) are refused before extraction; installed trees carry no group or other write and no setuid bit; the effective account and the enabled set follow the rules above, including a custom registry that enables an OPENAI route.
Permutations: consumer={usage only,cli only,both differing names,neither}; sources={codex,claude,claude2,opencode,gemini}; openai-route={absent,catalogued not enabled,enabled}; artifact={good,bad sha,wrong size,wrong version,incomplete inventory,hostile archive}; identity-input={version,hash,wrapper revision,node pin}

Title: AI CLI provisioning is transactional: staged, activated through an owned record, checked as the service account, reversible, and a no-op when converged
Requirement: Provisioning shall build each install only under a staging directory inside the prefix, delete the staging tree and the download at once on any failure, and publish by an atomic rename that never nests. Activation of a CLI (the /usr/local/bin link) shall be an owned transaction recorded in /var/lib/homehub-ai-clis/state.json as pending, checked, then committed, naming the previous link target, the previous target's version (the managed version, or for a hand-installed predecessor the version observed by running it once as the service account before the swap), the new wrapper and its version. Activation, rollback and recovery shall be ONE transaction primitive: the pending record (with the previous and the new target) is written durably (temp file, fsync, rename, directory fsync) BEFORE the swap and the operation aborts without swapping if that write fails; then swap, consumer check, checked, committed, and a failed write after the swap puts the link back. Retries shall be armed (the timer enabled) before any operation that can displace a link, including rollback and a recovery restore, and the timer shall be disabled only when no transaction for any CLI is open and no newer scheduling request exists, decided under a short lock that also covers the request stamp. The first time a managed install displaces an unowned link, a permanent baseline (its target and observed version) shall be written durably in the same write as the pending record and never replaced, so that rollback history never depends on a record that recovery can delete. Rollback is recorded the same way, including the removal that rolls back a first install, and recovery reconciles interrupted rollbacks too, even when provisioning is off or nothing is needed. A restore that cannot be verified keeps the record and returns non-zero; a link or an install directory that a link, a record or a wrapper refers to is never quarantined or deleted. At staging, after the swap, in recovery and in rollback, the same consumer check shall run: the CLI's --version, as the effective service account, in a fresh home, with only the units' PATH, under a timeout, expecting the exact pinned token; any failure shall restore the previous link automatically. A start shall reconcile only records left pending or checked; a link with no record shall never be touched, so hand-installed CLIs keep working until a managed activation succeeds. --rollback KEY shall swap to the recorded previous target and validate against the previous version (a first install, with no previous target, is rolled back by removing the managed link), and a failing check shall restore the current install. A converged re-run shall perform no network call and no write at all, state.json included.
Rationale: A half-finished activation is the failure that leaves a service pointing at a CLI nobody ever ran as the account that will run it. The Sol cross-review found that rollback validated against the wrong version, that recovery could touch links it did not own, and that a re-run could rewrite state; each is a clause here and a test below. The check runs as the account because a root-only pass proved nothing about the unit that fails at three in the morning.
AcceptanceCriteria: Kill points after the pending record, after the swap, after the check and after the checked record each recover on the next run to committed or to the previous link; an unrecorded link is never altered; a wrapper in a directory the account cannot read fails the post-swap, recovery and rollback checks and reverts; a hung CLI is cut off by the timeout; A then B then rollback validates A's version and a failing check restores B; rolling back a first install removes the link and succeeds; the wrapper of an older identity still runs the older CLI; the converged re-run leaves the inode, mtime and size of every file unchanged and calls curl zero times; a pending Gemini does not re-download completed CLIs; failure kinds (download, checksum, size, version, inventory, low disk, hostile archive) leave the hand-installed link, the bin directory, the staging area and the download directory exactly as they were.
Permutations: kill-point={after pending,after swap,after check,after checked}; predecessor={none,hand-installed,managed}; check={passes,wrong version,account cannot run,hangs}; rerun={converged,partly pending}; failure={download,checksum,size,version,inventory,low disk,hostile archive}

Title: AI CLI provisioning failure is visible and self-healing: its own supervised unit, a retry timer, a pending state, a disk reserve and a scheduler that never blocks
Requirement: Provisioning shall run as its own oneshot unit (homehub-ai-clis-provision.service, 3600 s start timeout) so first boot never waits on a download: first boot and the running-hub deploy call only provision-ai-clis.sh --schedule, which makes no network call, installs the two unit files, renders the retry interval, enables homehub-ai-clis-provision.timer first and only then starts the service with --no-block, and never waits on the artifact lock (enable and start touch only units; clearing pending state takes the lock with a non-blocking attempt and defers when it is busy). The run shall keep an aggregate deadline of 2400 s checked between artifacts (so that the deadline, one 900 s download and the staging margin fit the unit's 3600 s start timeout), exit 3 when anything is still owed (the timer stays enabled and retries every AI_CLI_PROVISION_RETRY_MINUTES, default 15, clamped to 5..1440, via a rendered drop-in), exit 0 and disable the timer when everything converged and no newer scheduling request arrived during the run (a --schedule leaves a durable stamp that the run compares against the one it started with), exit 2 on a refused configuration, and do nothing but disable the timer when AI_CLI_PROVISION is off or no enabled consumer needs a CLI. Every download shall use curl with --fail, --connect-timeout 20 and --max-time 900 over https only. A download shall be admitted only with free space of at least three times the artifact plus a 4096 MB reserve on both the temp directory and the prefix. A pending reason shall be printed once per change (then 'still pending since'), and --status shall report PROVISIONING: complete, INCOMPLETE with the key, the reason and the retry interval, running, or off, and --status --json shall give the machine-readable form recorded as IF-038.
Rationale: A retry that nobody can see, or one that fills the disk on every attempt, teaches people to ignore the box. The failure the Owner objected to was an opaque error code about packages; the replacement has to be a plain sentence that says what is owed and that the box is already retrying. Firstboot has a 1800 s budget and a download can take longer than that on a poor link, so the long work lives in a unit systemd supervises.
AcceptanceCriteria: --schedule makes no curl call and enables the timer before starting the service with --no-block; it returns within seconds while a long run holds the lock and a busy lock defers pending cleanup; exit 3 keeps the timer and exit 0 disables it; an empty needed set or AI_CLI_PROVISION=off disables it and clears pending; the interval drop-in carries the clamped value for 1, 5, 30, 1440, 99999, text and blank; a persistent checksum or version failure keeps the timer and prints its message once; a zero deadline yields exit 3 with no download; every curl call carries --fail, --connect-timeout 20, --max-time 900 and --proto =https; repeated persistent failures on a small tmpfs leave free space unchanged and a low-space reserve blocks the download; --status and --status --json report the documented shape in the states complete, incomplete, running and off.
Permutations: mode={schedule,run,check,status,status-json,rollback}; exit={0,2,3}; provision={auto,off}; needed-set={empty,non-empty}; lock={free,held by a long run}; retry-knob={1,5,30,1440,99999,text,blank}; space={ample,below reserve,small tmpfs}

Title: AI CLI service account and unit wiring: one effective account for both consumers, the Codex home always present, first boot only schedules, updaters suppressed
Requirement: Both consumers of the AI CLIs shall run as one effective service account: AI_CLI_USER when AI_CLI_ENABLED is true, otherwise AI_USAGE_USER_ACCOUNT. When both are enabled with different names, setup shall not refuse; the usage unit's User and Group drop-in, the Codex-home ownership, REFRESH_HOME, every refresher drop-in and the printed recipes shall all use the effective account, and one log line shall name it. A shared ensure-ai-account.sh (unprivileged, no sudo or docker, real shell; hub and root refused) shall create or certify it, and first boot, setup-ai-cli.sh, setup-ai-usage.sh and the running-hub path shall all call it. /var/lib/homehub-ai-codex shall be created empty, owned by the effective account, mode 0700, whenever the usage unit is installed, because the unit lists it in ReadWritePaths unconditionally. First boot shall call only provision-ai-clis.sh --schedule when either consumer is enabled. Updater suppression shall be installed and verified by effective setting where the vendor can report one (claude managed-settings, gemini system settings, opencode config), and recorded unproven where it cannot.
Rationale: Two differently named accounts collide on StateDirectory ownership, and a missing Codex home fails the usage unit's namespace setup before the feeder runs. The Owner's direction was that the deployers prepare what the configuration needs; creating the account and the directory is part of that. A vendor updater replacing a pinned binary would make every identity and checksum decorative.
AcceptanceCriteria: A CLI-only deployment creates and certifies its account and not the default usage account; a usage-only deployment uses its own name; with both enabled and differing names exactly one account is used throughout and both unit files' User agree; hub and root are refused; setup-ai-usage.sh no longer exits 2 on an absent account; a fresh usage install with AI_USAGE_SOURCES=claude,gemini creates the Codex home 0700 owned by the effective account (the path is read from the real unit file); the first-boot block calls --schedule when either consumer is enabled and never waits; the updater files parse with the exact keys and the verification either reports the effective setting or records unproven.
Permutations: consumers={usage only,cli only,both same,both differing}; account={absent,present,hub,root}; sources={with codex,without codex}; updater-query={available,unavailable}

Title: AI CLI two-level status: installed versus consumer-verified, each login separately, credential paths that match what sign-in writes
Requirement: The status step shall report per CLI an INSTALLED level (provisioned, committed, version matches) and a CONSUMER OPERATION VERIFIED level (the real consumer did its job under its real unit), never conflated, and shall read provisioning from provision-ai-clis.sh --status --json. It shall list each Codex home separately and only for active consumers: the usage home when codex is in AI_USAGE_SOURCES, the ai-cli home only when an OPENAI-family route is enabled. It shall accept exactly the supported credential-path mappings for claude, claude2, gemini and opencode; any other value shall report unsupported-path with the exact default path as the fix and never the word blank. The login check shall run as the account without reading content, and shall give one of: login owed, permissions wrong (owner, mode and the exact fix, no login recipe), credential present (not verified), verified; for Gemini it shall also require the oauth-personal auth type and say which is wrong. Recipes shall name /usr/local/bin and list only sources that are unverified and permission-correct. No output shall print credential content or describe a CLI as a missing package.
Rationale: The feeder treats a blank credential knob as unset, so advice to leave it blank breaks it silently. A root-only credential file, or a Gemini signed in with an API key, reads as a login problem when it is a permission or auth-type problem, and the recipe that fixes one makes the other worse.
AcceptanceCriteria: Each supported mapping is accepted and each other value is unsupported-path with the exact default path; a feeder integration test resolves every credential knob from the default values; the login matrix covers root-owned 0600, missing, present and verified, and Gemini selectedType missing, gemini-api-key and oauth-personal; a canary credential never appears in output; the happy path contains none of missing, not found or refus; usage-only Codex shows one home, ai-cli-only with an OPENAI route shows the other, and no OPENAI route shows no ai-cli line.
Permutations: source={claude,claude2,gemini,opencode,codex}; path={default,other}; login={absent,root-owned 0600,present,verified}; gemini-auth={unset,gemini-api-key,oauth-personal}; openai-route={absent,enabled}

Title: Panel rings follow the AI-usage sources: gaugeRings derived from AI_USAGE_SOURCES at every boot, without touching an Owner-written block
Requirement: install-renderer-config.py shall, when AI_USAGE_ENABLED is true, derive the panel's gaugeRings block from AI_USAGE_SOURCES in the order claude, claude2, codex, grok, gemini, opencode, freellmapi filtered to the listed sources (unknown names appended in listed order), marking claude and claude2 with the claude mark and badging them 1 and 2 only when both are listed, with unlisted set to hide so membership follows the sources. The shipped default block, an absent block and a marker-carrying block shall be derivable; any other block is Owner-written and shall be left alone with one log line. The source copy of config.json and the .env are the authority; the tool shall never edit the source, shall replace the destination by a rename inside its directory so the directory inode is unchanged, shall be byte-identical on re-run, and shall never print a secret-class key. FreeLLMAPI is out of scope until a gateway knob exists.
Rationale: The panel read gaugeRings once at boot from a hub-served file, and the Owner approved deriving it from the same list that decides which feeders run, so adding a source to the hub no longer needs a second edit on the panel side.
AcceptanceCriteria: The output passes the real normalizeGaugeRings under node without loss; order is read from gauges.js; the cases codex,claude,opencode, five sources with badges, claude2 alone, a marker re-derived, an Owner-written hide block untouched, the shipped default derived, re-run byte-identical, source unmodified, destination directory inode unchanged, secret-class keys never printed, AI_USAGE_ENABLED=false byte-identical, and a dropped source leaving the slots all hold.
Permutations: sources={one,three,five,claude2 only,unknown name}; block={absent,default,marker,owner-written}; enabled={true,false}; rerun={first,repeat}

Title: Desktop S/PDIF relaunch delay resets after a healthy run
Requirement: The wall image shall relaunch wall-spdif-in's alsaloop from inside wall-alsaloop-guard.py (--respawn) on a schedule that returns to its first step, of at most two seconds, after any child run of at least the configured healthy duration, however many fast failures preceded it; consecutive fast failures shall walk a non-decreasing schedule capped at no more than 30 seconds; a stop request during a run or a backoff shall end the guard promptly and stop its child; a child that cannot be executed shall exit the guard non-zero so the unit's Restart= and SR-037's start limit remain the backstop. Panel-internal legs that share the guard shall keep exiting to systemd.
Rationale: Measured on the panel 2026-10-16: systemd's restart counter is not reset by a healthy run, so SR-037's RestartSteps ramp climbed during one bad patch and then charged every later glitch its 120-second ceiling; a crash at 20:22:16 after seventeen clean minutes left the desktop leg silent for 104 seconds, which contradicts SN-025's short-disruption criterion. The guard's internal relaunches are not unit starts, so SR-037's arithmetic is unaffected.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_wall_audio_reenumeration.py sr082 tests: the schedule ramps, holds, and resets after a healthy run; supervise() requests the measured delays between runs and ends at once on a stop during a run or a 30-second backoff; real child processes are relaunched until stopped; an unexecutable child exits 1; SIGTERM ends the loop and its child (POSIX); the unit's real ExecStart parses under the guard's real parser with respawn on, a first step of at most 2 s and a cap of at most 30 s; and no other guard user passes --respawn.
Permutations: run={healthy,fast-fail}; history={fresh,ramped,capped}; stop={during-run,during-backoff}; child={executable,missing}; unit={spdif,internal-leg}

Title: One capped log store and a low-disk alarm on the panel
Requirement: The wall image shall not run a classic syslog daemon on the panel: rsyslog.service and syslog.socket shall be disabled, stopped and masked at every boot, and journald shall be the only log store, with its SystemMaxUse and SystemKeepFree set explicitly and its forwarding to syslog turned off. The stock logrotate configuration and the rsyslog package's conffiles shall be left as shipped. The image shall measure available space on the root filesystem and, when it is a separate filesystem, the media cache at the path firstboot resolved from WALL_MEDIA_CACHE, every 15 minutes, writing a warning-priority `wall-disk: LOW` journal line for any mount whose available bytes are below the smaller of 10 % of its size and 5 GB and replacing /run/wall-disk/status.json with {schemaVersion, observedAt, ttlMs, low, mounts[{label, path, mount, freeBytes, totalBytes, thresholdBytes, low}]}. All of it is installed, enabled and started by wall-firstboot.sh on every boot, so the paired release lane carries it, and no failure in it may stop a later firstboot step: each is reported as a failed step and firstboot continues.
Rationale: Measured 2026-10-18 00:02: the weekly logrotate gzipped a /var/log/syslog that had grown to tens of GB (syslog.2.gz is 944 MB compressed) and filled the panel's root for about two minutes; Chromium hit FILE_ERROR_NO_SPACE, its cookie store stopped persisting for the rest of that run, and a later kiosk restart lost the Pandora sign-in. Nothing capped rsyslog's file and nothing on the panel reported the disk filling. journald already holds every message under its own cap and nothing on the panel or in its sibling repositories reads /var/log/syslog, so the classic copy was a second, uncapped store. Rotating it harder was tried and rejected in review: replacing the package's logrotate conffile in place causes upgrade conflicts, and Debian policy forbids diverting conffiles. The panel has no alert route to the hub, so the alarm is the journal line plus a status file the panel app can surface later. The root is 98 GB and the panel runs on mains power.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_wall_disk_and_log_cap.py: fake df output parses, the threshold is the smaller of 10 % and 5 GB, exactly-at-threshold is not low, a cache still on root is reported once, unparseable df output is refused, a failed df exits 1 and leaves the previous status file, a non-default cache path from the environment is the one measured; main() writes the status file atomically with a two-period ttlMs; the journald caps are explicit; the firstboot block disables rsyslog, masks rsyslog.service and syslog.socket with --now and checks both inactive, is idempotent across two runs (no disable of an already-masked unit), skips a unit that does not exist, ships and changes no logrotate configuration, undoes the earlier draft's conffile diversion and hourly drop-in if present, writes the resolved cache path (refusing a non-absolute or whitespace path), restarts journald only when its drop-in changed, enables, restarts and checks active the disk timer, and a failing mask, a unit still active, a failing install, a failing enable or an inactive timer is a failed step with every later step still run.
Permutations: df={root low by 10 % arm; media low by 5 GB arm; both ok; cache on root; at threshold; unparseable; df failed}; syslog units={active; already masked; rsyslog absent; mask fails; still active}; earlier draft={absent; diversion and drop-in present}; journald drop-in={changed; unchanged}; install/enable={ok; fails}; WALL_MEDIA_CACHE={default; non-default; unusable}

Title: Touch-filter protection survives a reboot: a private state directory, deleted by OFF, carried by firstboot
Requirement: The wall image shall give wall-touch-filter.service a private persistent state directory, StateDirectory=wall-touch-filter (/var/lib/wall-touch-filter, root, mode 0700), and shall make nothing else writable: ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome, PrivateTmp and the single ReadWritePaths=/run/wall-touch-filter are unchanged. The application keeps its last qualifying fault renewal there and restores it at start (OfficeWallNaglight touchfilter/persist.py, WSN-099). TOUCH_FILTER_MODE=off shall delete the persisted protection (protection.json) and nothing else in the directory. The unit shall reach the panel only through configure-touch-filter.sh, which wall-firstboot.sh runs on every boot, so a system-lane paired release and a reimage carry the same unit.
Rationale: Measured 2026-10-21: protection lived only in memory and /run, so the 22:41 power-off reset it, and a column fault that fires one phantom every 20-60 s went natively to the kiosk again until it was re-detected. A state directory is the narrowest grant that survives a reboot: systemd creates it with the mode, owns its lifetime and adds it to the writable set under ProtectSystem=strict itself. OFF is the SSH recovery path, so it must not leave a band to resurrect when adaptive is turned back on. The paired lane's system manifest is derived from firstboot, and a file only user-data installs never changes on a live panel (HomeHub auto-memory release-lane-carries-only-firstboot-installs).
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_touch_filter_persistence.py: the unit carries StateDirectory=wall-touch-filter once with StateDirectoryMode=0700, its only ReadWritePaths is /run/wall-touch-filter, ProtectSystem=strict, no other *Directory= or path grant; the helper's real OFF branch (systemctl and udevadm stubbed) deletes protection.json and leaves any other file; no other branch names the file; firstboot runs the helper, the helper installs the unit from the payload before daemon-reload and user-data does not mention it; with the sibling app, the daemon's default state directory is /var/lib/<StateDirectory> and the file OFF deletes is the file persist.py writes.
Permutations: unit={StateDirectory; mode; ReadWritePaths; sandbox}; mode={off; shadow/filter/adaptive}; state dir={file present; other file present}; delivery={firstboot; user-data}

Title: One hub alert path: ntfy, rate-limited per key, journaled, once per episode
Requirement: The hub shall raise every host-side monitoring alert through one helper (stack/monitoring/homehub-alert.sh) that reads NTFY_BIND_IP (else LAN_IP), NTFY_PORT and HOMEHUB_ALERT_TOPIC from the stack .env as text, posts to ntfy under a hard timeout, suppresses a key DELIVERED less than its repeat window ago (stamping only on delivery, ignoring a stamp more than a minute in the future), and writes exactly one journal line per call whatever happened. rustdesk-check.sh shall use it with its existing stamps and behaviour unchanged. Each monitor shall alert once when a condition starts and once when it clears, retrying an alert that was not delivered while the condition lasts, and sending a clear only for an episode whose start was delivered. Each monitor run shall write its record and save its episode state, with every owed alert marked pending, before attempting any alert; shall spend at most one delivery budget per run that ends at least 10 s before its unit's TimeoutStartSec; and shall leave any alert the budget cannot reach pending for the next run.
Rationale: rustdesk-check.sh carried the only alert transport on the hub; four new monitors each growing a copy would drift. ntfy can be down exactly when the hub is in trouble, so the journal line must be the record and an undelivered alert must be retried rather than lost. ntfy is a local container and is slowest exactly when the hub is overloaded, and the alarms are correlated (a thermal event raises three at once): serial alerts before the save could outlast the unit's timeout, and a killed run saves nothing, so the next run would be killed the same way for the whole incident. A per-sample alert would flood the topic; a per-episode alert is what a person can act on.
AcceptanceCriteria: Hermetic: a stub curl sees one POST with the topic URL, Title and Priority; a second call with the same key inside the window exits 3 with no POST while another key goes out; a failing curl exits 4, journals ALERT NOT DELIVERED and writes no stamp, and the next call posts; missing config journals ALERT NOT SENT; a future stamp is ignored; a bad key or priority is refused; a CR/LF title cannot inject a header; a hung curl returns within its timeout. The episode machine fires once, clears once, retries undelivered fires and clears, and treats a suppressed fire as unsent. The rustdesk-check suite passes with the helper in place. Four simultaneous telemetry alarms against a hung ntfy, through the real helper and deadline, finish inside the unit timeout with the sample appended and all four alerts pending; the state is on disk, pending, before the first attempt in every monitor.
Permutations: delivery={delivered; ntfy down; no config; no curl; hung}; rate limit={first; inside window; other key; window 0; future stamp}; episode={start; continue; clear; flap; fire undelivered; clear undelivered; suppressed}

Title: Hub telemetry record with thermal, throttle and frequency alarms
Requirement: The hub shall append one JSON record every 30 s to /var/lib/homehub-telemetry/telemetry-YYYYMMDD.jsonl holding every thermal zone, every hwmon temperature, each core's current frequency, CPU busy since the previous sample, the summed core and package throttle counters, the load average, PSI and the usage of every filesystem on the NVMe, retaining the newest 7 day files and at most 50 MiB (never deleting the file being written, never appending past the cap), with export and summary commands. On each sample it shall alarm when the hottest CPU sensor or the NVMe exceeds its knob limit for N consecutive samples (clearing after N samples 5 C below), when the throttle counters increase (clearing after a quiet count), and when every core is below a frequency floor while the CPU is at least a busy percentage, for N samples. Consecutive counts use the monotonic clock and boot id: a reboot or a gap over four periods restarts them; a missing sensor is recorded null and advances nothing; a counter that decreases is a new baseline.
Rationale: Nothing on the hub recorded temperatures, frequency or throttling, so a cooling fault or a box held at its floor clock would leave no trace. The panel has kept the equivalent since 2026-09-14 (WSN-036), and the same retention keeps the disk bounded. Retention by day-file count rather than wall-clock age, and counting on the monotonic clock, keep a clock jump from deleting real records or faking a run of samples.
AcceptanceCriteria: Hermetic: a fake sysfs/procfs tree yields every field, a sensor without data reads null, a filesystem not on the NVMe is never statfs'd; each rule fires after its N samples and clears (with hysteresis for temperatures); a missing sensor neither fires nor clears; a throttle counter reset is a baseline; the frequency rule needs load; a reboot and a ten-minute gap restart the count; rotation keeps 7 files and the cap and never the active file, including after a clock jump; torn lines are skipped by export; a full disk (a real /dev/full on Linux) exits 1 and still saves the rules state; four samples over the limit alert exactly once.
Permutations: sensor={present; no data; absent}; rule={cpu temp; nvme temp; throttle; freq floor}; sequence={below N; at N; hysteresis band; clear}; boot={same; new}; gap={30 s; 10 min}; files={under 7; over 7; over cap; active oldest}; write={ok; ENOSPC}

Title: Hub low-disk alarm on NVMe filesystems only
Requirement: Every 15 minutes the hub shall measure the mount points listed in HOMEHUB_DISK_MOUNTS (default / /var/lib/docker /boot; each optionally PATH=N% or PATH=NG), statfs'ing a path only when /proc/self/mountinfo shows it mounted and its block device resolves through sysfs (including device-mapper slaves) to the NVMe, and judge it LOW when its available bytes are below its floor, by default the smaller of 10 % of its size and 5 GB. It shall alert once per crossing and once on recovery, alert when a configured path is not a mount point, report a path on any other device as skipped without touching it, write one journal line per mount and /var/lib/homehub-monitor/disk-status.json with a timestamp, and exit 0 whenever it ran.
Rationale: A full root on the box that serves the LAN's DNS fails rather than degrades (firstboot step 1b). The USB backup and library drives spin down and must never be woken by a monitor; their free space belongs to the backup run's own record. The scratch volume (plan W4a) joins by configuration, not code.
AcceptanceCriteria: Hermetic: specs parse and malformed ones are refused; the default floor is 5 GB on a 100 GB volume and 10 % on a 2 GB one; a USB mount is skipped and never statfs'd; an unmounted configured path alerts; a crossing alerts once, stays quiet while low and alerts once on recovery; a 99% override fires on an otherwise healthy mount; real sysfs links classify an NVMe partition and LVM-on-NVMe as NVMe and LVM-on-USB, USB and virtual devices as not.
Permutations: device={nvme partition; dm over nvme; usb; dm over usb; virtual}; mount={mounted; absent}; free={above floor; below floor; recovered}; floor={default; N%; NG; malformed}

Title: Hub watched jobs from one table
Requirement: Every 5 minutes the hub shall judge each applicable row of stack/monitoring/watch.table - a process absent for its threshold (counted on the monotonic clock within a boot), a systemd unit with no successful finish for its threshold (systemd's record, kept across reboots in the watch's state; a last run that failed is no success since it started), or any container docker reports unhealthy for its threshold (one alert per container), or any container whose restart count rose by three or more within its threshold (a crash loop never reads unhealthy) - and alert once when a watch fires and once when it clears. The table shall carry the IceDrive client (ICEDRIVE_MODE=appimage, absent 15 min), the library backup and the IceDrive profile capture (no success for 26 h), unhealthy containers (10 min) and a drill-only synthetic process watch named by a knob; rows shall be switchable off by HOMEHUB_WATCH_DISABLE. Two further kinds (plan W3b): a newest-file watch, bad when the newest regular file matching an absolute glob with a fixed root has an mtime THRESHOLD old or older, or when nothing has matched for THRESHOLD since the watch first saw the tree empty, never following a symlink and bounded in entries and time (hitting a bound is bad); and a scratch-identity watch, bad when stack/scratch/homehub_scratch.py's own `status`, run under a timeout, does not report mounted, identity_ok and prjquota all true - or cannot run, times out or prints no JSON - on every run for THRESHOLD. The table shall also carry, each gated by its component's switch: the door recorder's newest segment /srv/scratch/door/*/door-*.ts* (the open .ts.part included) older than 15 min (DOOR_RECORDER_ENABLED=true), the scratch volume's identity for 5 min (HOMEHUB_SCRATCH_ENABLED=true) and homehub-meeting-pull.service with no success for 30 min (MEETING_PULL_ENABLED=true), each threshold a knob a drill may set to 0 (fires at the next run) in the monitors' override file. When /proc, systemctl or docker cannot answer, the row is unknown and nothing changes; a file walk or a scratch status that cannot answer is bad, never unknown. The watch starts and stops nothing.
Rationale: The offsite sync client was down for most of 2026-09-19..10-21 and nothing noticed. One table keeps adding a watch to a line of data; a synthetic watch lets the alert path be proved end to end without stopping anything real. The door recorder, the scratch volume and the meeting pull (HomeHub plan W3b) each fail silently otherwise: a recorder that stops writing, a writer volume mounted from the wrong device, a pull that never succeeds. The scratch watch asks the guard's own module, so the watch and the writers' guard can never disagree about what the right volume is.
AcceptanceCriteria: Hermetic: the shipped table parses with no problems and honours each condition and the disable list; malformed rows are reported, not guessed; a process watch fires at its threshold, clears when the process returns and restarts on a reboot; a unit-success watch ages a stored success across a lost systemd record, is stale at once after an old failed run, and judges a never-run unit from first sight; container watches are per container and unknown when docker hangs; the synthetic drill fires once and clears once end to end. W3b (tests/test_hub_monitoring.py -k 'tc1460 or tc1461 or tc1462 or tc1463 or tc1464 or tc1465', stack/monitoring/tests/monitoring.test.sh TC-1466): the three rows are absent without their knobs and take 0m overrides; the door watch fires on a stale tree, counts the open .ts.part, fires on an empty or missing tree after the threshold from first sight, follows no symlinked root, directory or file, and fires when its walk hits the entry or time bound; the scratch watch reads homehub_scratch.status()'s own keys, fires on the second bad run in a row and on a status that crashes, times out or prints no JSON; each drill fires once and clears once through main(); on Linux the real tree with links out and the real scratch status fire as expected.
Permutations: kind={process; unit-success; docker-health; docker-restarts; newest-file; scratch-identity}; observation={present; absent; success; failed; never ran; unknown}; boot={same; new}; table={shipped; malformed; disabled row; condition false}; tree={fresh; stale; open .part only; empty; missing; symlink out; over the entry bound; walk stuck}; scratch status={ok; not mounted; wrong device; no prjquota; uuid unset; crashes; times out; no JSON}; drill={door 0m; scratch tool absent at 0m; meeting pull 0m}

Title: Hub liveness probe with one bounded, redacted evidence bundle per incident
Requirement: Every 60 s the hub shall ask Technitium on the LAN address for a configured local name over UDP (NOERROR or NXDOMAIN is an answer), Caddy on 127.0.0.1:443 for any HTTP status over TLS with that SNI, and docker for `docker ps` under a timeout. After HOMEHUB_LIVENESS_FAILURES consecutive failed runs it shall write exactly one evidence bundle for the incident to /var/lib/homehub-evidence/<UTC ts>/ (root, 0700, files 0600) - processes by comm only, top, PSI, meminfo, D-state stacks, the dmesg tail, the last 10 minutes of the journal for a named list of units and tags, docker names and states, docker stats, the failing checks and a manifest - and then alert; the first passing run ends the incident and alerts once. Each command runs under a timeout that kills its process group; the bundle has a whole-capture deadline, per-file and per-bundle byte caps, and pruning to the newest 20 bundles and 64 MiB by capture sequence, never the new bundle; every item that fails, times out, is truncated, skipped or cannot be written (ENOSPC), and every failed prune, is recorded in the manifest and the capture continues. Every captured line passes the secrets-floor redactor before it is written. The probe never acts.
Rationale: The 2026-10-04 wedge left no record. The panel's freeze bundles are how panel faults get diagnosed; the hub's must be captured before anything else happens, independent of the opt-in recovery supervisor's path, and must not themselves fill the disk, hang on a dead docker or leak a credential from a log.
AcceptanceCriteria: Hermetic: DNS packets round-trip and SERVFAIL, a wrong id and a short reply are failures; a closed HTTPS port fails; the incident machine opens once at the threshold and closes on the first pass; six failing runs write one bundle and one urgent alert, recovery sends one clear, and a new incident gets a new bundle; a bundle holds every item with root-only modes; a docker that blocks for ever times out per item with its process group killed; the deadline skips what it cannot reach; a flooding journal is cut at the caps; ENOSPC on two items is recorded while the rest are written; pruning keeps 20 and the byte cap by sequence; a failed prune is recorded; planted GitHub, OpenAI-style, bearer and password values are redacted and counted; no monitor holds an argv that restarts, stops or kills anything.
Permutations: check={dns ok; dns servfail; dns silent; https ok; https refused; docker ok; docker hung}; incident={below threshold; open; continue; close; reopen}; item={ok; timeout; failed; truncated; skipped-deadline; skipped-bundle-cap; write-failed}; prune={under caps; over count; over bytes; fails}; content={clean; token; bearer; password; private key}

Title: The wall image carries the panel's compositor freeze watchdog
Requirement: The wall image shall carry the panel's freeze watchdog - wall-freeze-watch.sh, wall-freeze-watch.service and its env file with RECOVER=1 - byte-identical to the copies hand-installed on the panel on 2026-09-15, install all three on every firstboot (script 0755 to /usr/local/sbin, unit to /etc/systemd/system, env to /etc/wall-panel/freeze-watch.env), enable and start the service when WALL_FREEZE_WATCH_ENABLED is true (the default), restart it only when one of its files changed, and stop and disable it when the knob is false while leaving the files installed. A knob that is neither true nor false is a failed step and the watchdog stays on.
Rationale: Three wedges on 2026-09-15 left no log line; the watchdog that captures their forensics was hand-installed and in no repository, so a reimage would have silently dropped it. Byte-identical payloads mean the paired release's system lane takes the live files over in place without restarting a watchdog in the middle of counting failures.
AcceptanceCriteria: The payload files' sha256 equal the hashes read from the panel on 2026-10-22; RECOVER=1; the script is executable in git and in the archive the release ships; the firstboot block, executed with stubs, installs the three files, enables the unit without a restart when unchanged, restarts it when changed, disables it (files kept) when the knob is false, and fails the step on a bad knob; the install lines keep the form the release manifest generator reads.
Permutations: knob={unset; true; false; invalid}; files={unchanged; changed}

Title: Hub monitoring installed by firstboot behind one knob per component
Requirement: Firstboot shall (re)install the four monitoring units and timers from stack/monitoring on every boot and converge each timer to its knob - HOMEHUB_TELEMETRY_ENABLED, HOMEHUB_DISK_CHECK_ENABLED, HOMEHUB_WATCH_ENABLED, HOMEHUB_LIVENESS_ENABLED - enabling it (with --now) when the knob is true or unset, disabling it when false, and leaving it unchanged with a warning for any other value. Every unit shall be a bounded oneshot (CPUQuota, MemoryMax, TasksMax, TimeoutStartSec) driven by its timer, never a respawning daemon. Each monitor shall read its knobs from the stack .env with /etc/homehub-monitor/override.env laid over it, so a drill never edits the stack's .env. Their dependencies (python3, procps, util-linux, curl) are in the base image and packages.list, so an enabled knob needs nothing provisioned.
Rationale: Each component is evidence, like the always-on hub-pressure record, so a hub reimaged from a .env that predates them should not come up blind; a knob still lets any one be switched off. Bounding every unit keeps a monitor from being the reason the hub is slow.
AcceptanceCriteria: Static: every unit is a bounded oneshot with its timer cadence; firstboot installs all eight unit files and converges each timer to its knob; .env.example declares every knob a monitor reads. Executed: the converger enables for true and unset, disables for false, and touches nothing for an invalid value. validate_config.py finds every shipped unit installed by firstboot.
Permutations: knob={unset; true; false; invalid}; component={telemetry; disk; watch; liveness}

Title: One press of the panel's power button never shuts it down; two within 5 s do
Requirement: The wall image shall run wall-power-button.service, which holds logind's handle-power-key block inhibitor (systemd-inhibit --what=handle-power-key --mode=block --who=wall-power-button wrapping the daemon) for exactly as long as the daemon runs, and restarts after any exit. The daemon shall read every input device named exactly "Power Button", count EV_KEY KEY_POWER value 1 only (releases and autorepeat are not presses), and treat a press on a different device than the last counted press within 150 ms of it as the same physical press, while two presses on the same device are always two. A first press shall begin a 5 s window (WSN-098's warning, SR-094); a second counted press at or before the window's end shall run systemctl poweroff; a press after it begins a new window. A failed or stalled (60 s) poweroff returns the guard to idle with an alert. The kiosk being unavailable shall change none of this. firstboot installs and starts it on every boot when WALL_POWER_BUTTON_GUARD=true (the default) and then requires the inhibitor in systemd-inhibit --list; false disables it and logind's default applies.
Rationale: Ruled by the Owner 2026-10-22 (OfficeWallNaglight WSN-098) after measurement: the button reports press and release at the same instant on event4 (EV_KEY 116 value 1 then 0) for a short press and a 3 s hold alike, so a hold cannot be detected and the original hold-to-shut-down design is impossible. The inhibitor is held by a wrapper around the daemon rather than by the daemon itself, so no code path in the daemon can drop it while it runs, and any exit hands the button back to logind's default (one press powers off): the button is never dead. Firmware forces power off on a long hold (about 4 s or more) whatever software does; that is unchanged.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_wall_power_button.py TC-1315..TC-1327: one press then timeout publishes armed then idle with no poweroff; two presses 0.5-5.0 s apart run poweroff once; two presses 6 s apart are two warnings; one press on two devices within 150 ms counts once (and the echo of a second press too); two presses on one device 0-299 ms apart count twice; autorepeat, release, SYN and other keys are ignored; start publishes idle and the first press only warns; no acknowledgement raises the kiosk-unavailable alert and a blind double press still shuts down; a failed or stalled poweroff stands down; the unit wraps the daemon in the inhibitor, restarts always and keeps no state across a stop; logind's kiosk.conf leaves the power key and inhibitor handling at their defaults; the firstboot block installs, starts, restarts a changed unit and fails the step when no inhibitor is listed.
Permutations: presses={one; two inside 5 s; two 6 s apart; quick double on one device; one press on two devices; autorepeat}; service={running; started with a press; poweroff fails; poweroff stalls; a device vanishes}; kiosk={acknowledges; never paints}; WALL_POWER_BUTTON_GUARD={unset; true; false; invalid}; firstboot={unchanged; changed unit; install fails; enable fails; no inhibitor listed}

Title: The first press reaches the kiosk as a readable warning, or is reported
Requirement: On each first press the daemon shall replace /run/wall-power-button/state.json (IF-067) with {schemaVersion 1, state armed, seq, windowMs 5000, deadline, observedAt}, and with state shutting-down or idle when those happen; the directory is the unit's RuntimeDirectory, so a stopped service leaves no document. It shall ask wall-sleep.sh's power-button-wake arm, off the press path, to light a dark display through the image's one power-policy script; on a lit display that arm changes nothing but its wake stamp, which makes a display-off queued behind the power lock decline; on either it writes a 6 s hold during which wall-sleep.sh refuses every backlight-off (display-off, occupancy, sleep window), so the warning cannot be blanked while it is up. The kiosk acknowledges a warning it painted by writing {seq} to /run/wall-panel-renderer/power-warning-ack.json; no matching acknowledgement within 2 s, or a failed wake, journals a warning-priority ALERT line and then, off the press path, hands it to the panel's alert route /usr/local/lib/wall-panel/panel-alert, which posts it to the hub's ntfy through the hub's own alert helper (homehub-alert.sh, SR-085) at the address firstboot renders from wall.env's HUB_IP or, for a wall.env that predates that knob, from the single IPv4 nameserver in the panel's installed netplan (the same deploy value); when the route is missing, unconfigured or cannot reach the hub, a second line says ALERT NOT DELIVERED and nothing else changes.
Rationale: WSN-098 requires the warning to appear when the screen is dimmed or off, and the panel's display has one owner (wall-sleep.sh, SR-020/LLR-913), so the wake goes through it rather than a second writer. The hub's shared alert helper (SR-085, HomeHub plan W3a) is the one alert transport, so the panel ships a byte-identical copy and a small adapter rather than a second transport; ntfy is published on the hub's LAN address, which the panel reaches. Delivery never sits on the press path, so a hung or unreachable hub cannot stop a blind double press.

Title: AI-usage feeder: each source read on its own schedule, backing off when a vendor objects
Requirement: The feeder shall keep, per source (each Claude account is a source), a schedule in its state file - last attempt, next due time, whether that is a vendor Retry-After, backoff level, the authentication history of SR-068 and the last rate-limit response headers - under one reserved key with its own validator, and a cycle shall SKIP a source that is not due or is backing off. A skip is its own outcome: the source is not read, its gauges are not posted, and its schedule is unchanged. The interval is a knob per source (AI_USAGE_<SOURCE>_INTERVAL, 60..600 s, refused otherwise at --check); the default is 60 s, and 120 s for Codex. On an HTTP 429 or 5xx (or Codex's upstream 429) the source shall honour Retry-After in both its seconds and HTTP-date forms, a delay longer than ten minutes as given (clamped only at 24 h), and otherwise back off exponentially from its interval to a 10-minute ceiling; each backoff is journalled with the source named and the vendor's rate-limit headers. A source in backoff keeps its last reading with its true observed_at. A schedule entry stamped in the future is dropped (a clock that stepped back). The Codex read shall leave no process behind. The status step shall judge a source a run skipped by the newest earlier completed run that read it.
Rationale: Owner 2026-10-22: update the usage gauges every minute. None of the four endpoints publishes a rate limit and two are internal endpoints the vendors' own clients use, so ten times the requests has to be designed against: a source a vendor throttles must slow down on its own without slowing the others. The feeder is a one-shot unit, so the schedule must live in the state file. Codex's default is longer by measurement: one read's app-server tree cost 1.5 s of CPU of a 3.1 s cycle (4.2 s when it timed out, with over a hundred lsb_release children), and every second cycle still meets SR-096's freshness target; a long-lived supervised app-server was rejected because its idle cost could not be measured without calling the vendor and it needs its own credential-reload logic. Not posting a skipped source leaves NagLight holding the body it was last sent, which is the truth at its true stamp.
AcceptanceCriteria: A 60-s source is read every cycle and Codex every second; the knob changes it and a malformed one is refused by name; a skip posts nothing, says why and changes nothing; a numeric and an HTTP-date Retry-After are honoured to the second, one longer than ten minutes as given; no Retry-After backs off 120, 240, 480, 600, 600; a success ends the backoff; only 429 and 5xx throttle; rate-limit headers are recorded and nothing else; a restart between cycles (a fresh module) honours the schedule; a clock stepping back or forward reads the source at once; the Codex read kills its grandchildren; the status step verifies a skipped source from the run that read it and stops at a run that died.
Permutations: source={claude;claude2;codex;gemini;opencode}; outcome={ok;auth;throttled;failure;pending;skip}; retry_after={none;seconds;http-date;>600s;>24h;past}; clock={steady;back;forward}; process={same;restarted}

Title: AI-usage gauges every minute: the timer, the freshness target, and a Claude token renewed before it lapses
Requirement: homehub-ai-usage.timer shall fire every minute (OnUnitActiveSec=1min) with AccuracySec at most 5 s and RandomizedDelaySec at most 10 s, still within a quarter of the tightest staleness horizon. At steady state the panel shall show each usage gauge with an observed_at no more than 3 minutes old at the 95th percentile. homehub-claude-refresh@.timer shall check every 4 minutes and run the CLI only when the access token has under 20 minutes left, has expired, or its expiry cannot be read; its gate shall be able only to add runs (every result but 'not due' runs the CLI), shall never write and shall never print the credential.
Rationale: Measured before (2026-10-22): the feeder half of the lag was p95 ~630 s (a 10-minute timer plus up to 90 s) and the panel half at most its 60-s locked poll (unlocked, NagLight's event stream repaints within a second), so the panel needed no change. The refresher used to run every 4 h on the belief that any CLI run renews the token; the journal showed 14 Claude 401s in 9 days, each 237-242 min after a refresher run and each cleared by the next, i.e. the CLI renews only near expiry - on a minute timer such a lapse would confirm an authentication failure (SR-068) that is not one.
AcceptanceCriteria: The shipped timer's interval, accuracy and delay are asserted, with the due slack covering their jitter; the worst healthy served age of every default fits the target; the refresher's period gives two checks inside the ten-minute confirmation and three inside the 20-minute lead; the gate exits 3 only for a token with more than 20 min left, and the unit's own shell line maps only 3 to a skip (crash, missing helper and run all pass); on the live hub for 24 h the cycles are ~60 s apart and the p95 freshness is within 3 minutes (Demonstration, recorded in FOLLOWUPS).
Permutations: timer={OnUnitActiveSec;AccuracySec;RandomizedDelaySec}; gate={not-due;lead;expired;implausible;unreadable;missing;crash}; account={claude;claude2}

Title: The tracker checks a bearer token on every /api/* POST, and every hub poster sends it
Requirement: The stack shall pass TRACKER_API_TOKEN to the tracker from the hub's one minted feed token (the value every poster already carries), and every hub-side poster to the tracker's /api/* shall attach that token as Authorization: Bearer from its own knob.
Rationale: Open-items C51 (2026-08-30): the tracker ran auth=false, so the trusted X-Forwarded-User header (a stable, public Google sub) was the only check on stack_default, and the minted token every feeder sends was verified by nothing. Setting it costs one compose line and no new secret.

Title: Sure is started by its own unit and switched by SURE_ENABLED, never by COMPOSE_PROFILES
Requirement: The hub shall start the four Sure services (web, worker, Postgres, Redis) only through homehub-sure.service, which passes --profile sure, and shall switch Sure with SURE_ENABLED, read as exactly `true`. `sure` shall not be named in COMPOSE_PROFILES: the template shall not ship it there, and the image bake and the local-image resolver shall refuse it and select the Sure images by SURE_ENABLED instead. firstboot shall install the unit on every run, enable it and queue (never await) its start when the knob is true, disable and stop it when the knob is off and the unit had been enabled, and touch no running Sure container when the unit was never enabled. The services keep restart: unless-stopped, and the unit shall not propagate a docker.service restart into a stop.
Rationale: firstboot runs on every boot and its bulk docker compose up -d is all-or-nothing: with sure in COMPOSE_PROFILES it waits on Sure's database and cache before DNS provisioning, Samba and recovery (Codex gpt-6.1-sol, 2026-10-18 Sure deploy review). The hub config dropped the profile that day, which left Sure with no owner, no reboot behaviour anyone had proven, and a bake that keyed on the profile and so silently stopped carrying the locally built fork, which has no registry to fall back to.
AcceptanceCriteria: The unit script reads the knob exactly (quoted and CRLF forms accepted, True/yes/empty refused, the last assignment wins), starts the four with no build and no pull, stops web and worker before their database and cache, and fails the unit on a compose failure. The unit Wants= (not Requires=) docker and is After= firstboot. firstboot's block, executed with stubs, enables and queues the start for true, leaves an absent knob with a never-enabled unit untouched, disables and queues the stop when the unit had been enabled, warns on a sure profile and never starts the unit blocking. The exporter adds --profile sure exactly when the knob is true and refuses a sure profile; the resolver builds the fork exactly then and refuses the profile. A lab reboot showing Sure back without the profile is a hardware/lab acceptance step, recorded as not yet run.
Permutations: knob={true,"true",true+CRLF,True,yes,false,empty,absent}; unit={never-enabled,enabled}; profiles={none,sure,ntfy+sure}; verb={condition,start,stop}; compose={ok,fails}

Requirement: wall-firstboot.sh shall install from the payload every systemd unit file that the wall autoinstall late-commands install, on every run, so that the paired release lane - which carries exactly what wall-firstboot installs - can update each of them on a live panel.
