Title: NVMe scratch volume: an 18 GiB ext4 LV with project quotas, created non-destructively
Requirement: The repo shall provide stack/scratch/homehub_scratch.py, whose `plan` (read-only) and `ensure` verbs create an LV `hub-scratch` of HOMEHUB_SCRATCH_SIZE_MIB (18432) in the volume group holding /, ext4 with the quota and project features (prjquota-only quota inode, -m 0, -i 65536, label hub-scratch, UUID HOMEHUB_SCRATCH_UUID when set), an fstab line by UUID with nofail,noatime,prjquota at /srv/scratch whose bare mount point is mode 000, and mount it. Each step shall ask its end state first and resume a half-done run, except one stopped between creating the LV and formatting it, which is refused: only an LV created in the same run is ever formatted. It shall STOP, changing nothing, when the VG would keep fewer free extents than HOMEHUB_SCRATCH_VG_RESERVE_MIB (4096) after the LV, and REFUSE (exit 4) on an LV it would have to resize, an existing hub-scratch LV on which blkid -p finds no signature, a device on which blkid -p finds any signature other than its own labelled ext4, its own label with another UUID, an fstab line for /srv/scratch it did not write, a mount point already mounted from another device, or a bare mount point that holds data. Firstboot shall run `ensure` after the docker LV step when HOMEHUB_SCRATCH_ENABLED=true, as a log line on every outcome and never a failure of the unit.
Rationale: Plan W4a (Owner 2026-10-22: use NVMe scratch for recording until a new drive is installed). The measured hub VG had 5949 free 4 MiB extents (23.24 GiB): 18 GiB takes 4608 and leaves 5.24 GiB. Shrinking an LV is the Owner's call; formatting a device that holds something is never automatic. A reimage recreates the volume because its writers refuse to start without it, and recreates it WITH the recorded UUID so the guard knob stays true; its data is scratch and is not meant to survive.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_hub_scratch.py: the measured hub numbers give 4608 extents and 5.24 GiB left; a short VG is a STOP with the numbers and no command run; an existing LV is never recreated; an existing LV with no signature is refused, not formatted; a foreign signature is never formatted; our label with another UUID, a foreign fstab line and a non-empty mount point are refused; plan runs nothing. stack/scratch/tests/scratch-fs.root-test.sh on a real loop-backed VG: STOP leaves no LV; ensure gives the LV, the features, the fstab line, prjquota and mode 000 underneath; a second ensure has no actions.
Permutations: vg={fits; short}; lv={absent; ours; ours-other-uuid; foreign-signature}; fstab={absent; ours; foreign}; mountpoint={empty; holds data; mounted elsewhere}

Title: The scratch mount guard every writer runs before it starts and before every new file
Requirement: `homehub_scratch.py guard --writer NAME` (and homehub_scratch.guard() for Python writers) shall pass only when /srv/scratch is a mount point, HOMEHUB_SCRATCH_UUID is set and well formed, /dev/disk/by-uuid/<that UUID> is the mounted device, the filesystem is ext4 mounted with prjquota, it is not read-only, the calling process does not hold CAP_SYS_RESOURCE, /srv/scratch/NAME is a real directory on that filesystem in NAME's quota project with inheritance, and a probe file can be created there; otherwise it shall refuse with one sentence naming the first failed condition. Every writer unit shall carry RequiresMountsFor=/srv/scratch, BindsTo= and After=srv-scratch.mount, the guard as ExecStartPre, CapabilityBoundingSet=~CAP_SYS_RESOURCE and no restart for a guard refusal; a writer container shall have no restart policy of its own and long-syntax bind mounts with create_host_path: false.
Rationale: When the volume is absent /srv/scratch is a directory on /, and a writer that opened a path there would fill the root filesystem of the box that serves the LAN's DNS. RequiresMountsFor covers the start; the identity check covers a wrong device; the per-file check covers an unmount between files. The kernel ignores quota hard limits for a CAP_SYS_RESOURCE holder (fs/quota/dquot.c ignore_hardlimit), so a root writer that kept it would write through its budget.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_hub_scratch.py: every failed condition refuses and names itself; all true is the only pass; an unreadable fact is a refusal; CapEff bit 24 is read. Root suite on a real ext4: refused with CAP_SYS_RESOURCE, passed without; read-only, another ext4 with the same label and nothing mounted are each refused; unmounted mid-run, the recorder stops before its next segment and writes nothing under the bare mount point.
Permutations: mount={absent; wrong device; tmpfs; no prjquota; read-only; ours}; uuid={unset; malformed; set}; caller={with CAP_SYS_RESOURCE; without}; dir={missing; symlink; other fs; wrong project; full; ok}

Title: Enforced budgets on the scratch volume: one hard project quota per writer, sized to keep a floor free
Requirement: After the filesystem is made, `ensure` shall read its usable space (statvfs f_blocks x f_frsize) and give door/, meetings/ and ottertube/ project ids 7101, 7102 and 7103 with inheritance and block hard limits of HOMEHUB_SCRATCH_QUOTA_<WRITER>_MIB (8192, 2048, 6144), reduced - ottertube first, then meetings, then door, none below HOMEHUB_SCRATCH_MIN_QUOTA_MIB (512) - until all three at their limits leave HOMEHUB_SCRATCH_FREE_FLOOR_MIB (2048) of the usable space free, and STOP if they cannot; it shall report the usable space, each granted limit and the space free at full. Limits are set through quotactl(2) and project ids through FS_IOC_FSSETXATTR, needing no quota-tools package. A writer that hits EDQUOT or ENOSPC shall stop cleanly and alert through stack/monitoring/homehub-alert.sh, never write elsewhere.
Rationale: Plan W4a.3: budgets enforced by the filesystem, not allocations a writer promises to respect: a runaway write hits EDQUOT. Metadata and the journal reduce the usable space, so the sizes come from the mounted filesystem, not the LV size.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_hub_scratch.py: budgets that fit are granted; ottertube is reduced first and the floor holds; meetings only after ottertube is at its minimum; a set that cannot fit is a STOP. Root suite at 1/28 scale: door and meetings each stop at their limit with EDQUOT while the other still writes; all three full still leave the floor; the guard reports a full writer; a CAP_SYS_RESOURCE holder writes through a full quota; status reads the limits back.
Permutations: usable={roomy; tight; too small}; writer={door; meetings; ottertube}; state={empty; at quota; all at quota}

Title: Door relay: the doorbell's one RTSP session re-served on the LAN, pinned, authenticated, video only
Requirement: The stack shall run go2rtc pinned by version and digest (stack/door/door-relay-image.pin; ${DOOR_RELAY_IMAGE} equal to it) as compose service door-relay with profiles [door-relay] and restart "no", host networking, read_only, cap_drop ALL and its config bound read-only with create_host_path: false, started only by homehub-door-relay.service when DOOR_RELAY_ENABLED=true (ExecCondition: otherwise a clean skip). Each start shall render the config to /run/homehub-door-relay/go2rtc.yaml (0600 root) from the stack .env: RTSP on LAN_IP:DOOR_RELAY_RTSP_PORT with the doorbell's own username and password as the consumer credential, the API on 127.0.0.1:DOOR_RELAY_API_PORT behind the same credential with local_auth, WebRTC/SRTP/RTMP disabled, one stream DOOR_RELAY_STREAM from DOOR_RELAY_UPSTREAM_HOST/PORT/PATH with the credential percent-encoded and #media=video, default_query video. A missing or malformed field shall refuse the start naming the key, never the value. The relay's output shall reach the journal only through `door_relay.py redact-run` (stdout and stderr merged, every spelling of the credential and the camera's host:port removed line by line, the child's exit status kept), and the container shall have no log driver, so docker keeps no copy. No Caddy route and no DNS name. `door_relay.py import-upstream` shall take the panel's in-use host/port/path/username/password as NUL-separated records on stdin into the .env, encoded as the materialiser encodes ($ doubled, whitespace quoted), printing key names only.
Rationale: The RemoBell S accepts one video connection and the panel's broker holds it, so a recorder or a hub-side detector can only exist behind a relay (plan W4b). Hub names: the panel's DOORBELL_RTSP_HOST becomes the relay at the cutover, so the hub's camera fields are DOOR_RELAY_UPSTREAM_* - one name with two values on two machines is the overloaded-name defect class. go2rtc's producer warns with the whole credentialed upstream URL whenever the camera drops (review round 1, reproduced against the pinned 1.9.14), and info is the level that records dropouts, so the output is filtered rather than silenced. go2rtc exempts loopback clients from API auth unless local_auth (measured 200 without, 401 with); RTSP bound to the LAN address is never local (measured 401 without the credential from the host itself).
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_door_relay.py: the rendered config names and binds every listener, both authenticated, video only, the credential encoded, written 0600; each bad field is refused by name with no value in the message; the secret reader undoes exactly the materialiser's encoding; import writes the five keys and keeps the rest, bad records leave the file untouched; pin == knob == compose image; the compose block and units carry the lifecycle rules. stack/door/tests/door-relay-lab.sh against a fake camera: exactly two listeners; 401 without or with a wrong credential and on the API; the probe sees h264 1536x1536; no log line carries the password; the relay run from its own unit lines with the camera killed under a consumer logs the dropout redacted, with no password or camera host:port in its output or in docker.
Permutations: listener={rtsp; api; webrtc; srtp; rtmp}; credential={none; wrong; right}; field={each upstream key: missing; malformed}; password chars={@, space, $, :, #}

Title: Door relay measurement and the cutover/rollback tooling
Requirement: door_relay.py shall provide: `probe` (a test consumer with the doorbell's credential: codec, size, packets; a pass only on exit 0, packets > 0 and exactly DOOR_RELAY_EXPECT_CODEC (h264) and DOOR_RELAY_EXPECT_SIZE (1536x1536)), `gate` (the hub half of the compatibility gate: readiness and geometry by the same verdict, two simultaneous consumers with exactly one established upstream session and one API producer, one consumer leaving with the upstream kept and the survivor's OWN ffmpeg -progress frame count rising over --progress-seconds and last rising at most 2.5 s before the window ends - the relay's per-consumer sender bytes are reported and decide nothing, because go2rtc counts a packet when it is queued, not when it is delivered - as JSON lines and an exit code), `streams` (API counts, URLs redacted), `upstream-count` (ss) and `cost` (cgroup CPU as percent of one core and PSI cpu some avg60 mean and max over a duration). stack/door/door-cutover-panel.sh shall provide the panel half: export-upstream (NUL records to stdout only), prepare (rollback material as the actual inputs - the DOORBELL_RTSP_* lines and every credential file - in /var/lib/wall-door-cutover/<UTC>/ 0700, checksums only printed), suppress (runtime mask and stop, process gone), point, restore, regenerate (wall-firstboot.sh, verified by artifact), compare, release, probe (broker live on HOST:PORT, peers by address; exit 0 only when the broker reported live AND HOST:PORT was a peer while it was live) and compat (the installed broker's own ffconcat input and ffmpeg arguments against a target, its SECONDS enforced by select() and never by a blocking read, the decoder always killed on the way out, and exit 0 only when frames arrived without a stall or an early end). No verb prints a secret; URLs in any relayed line are redacted. Every consumer the hub runs (probe, the gate's consumers, the cost decoder and the SR-107 recorder) shall receive the relay's authenticated URL only as a one-entry ffconcat document on its stdin (ffmpeg/ffprobe as the container entrypoint, -f concat -i pipe:0, docker run -i), so the credential is in no argv, no container environment and no file.
Rationale: Plan W4b tasks 8, 10 and 11: the camera takes one connection, so the gate runs in a planned window with the broker suppressed; the transaction must be reversible with the actual inputs, not checksums; and the hub's cost must be measured before moving detection.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_door_relay.py: redaction and the upstream count; the gate fails a failed probe, an altered codec or geometry and a survivor whose own frame count is flat or silent while the relay's counters rise; every consumer's argv carries no URL, no credential spelling, no shell and no env, and its document reaches stdin. door-relay-lab.sh checks 4b and 4c: a survivor SIGSTOPped before or just after the first sample fails the real gate; check 11: no running consumer has the credential in /proc cmdline or environ or in docker inspect. door-cutover-panel.test.sh runs the probe and compat bodies against fakes: never-live and peer-before-only probes fail; a silent stream ends at the deadline with the decoder killed. stack/door/tests/door-relay-lab.sh: the gate passes against a fake single-session camera; the panel broker's ffconcat input path produces JPEG frames from the relay.
Permutations: consumers={1; 2; one leaves}; verb={each}

Title: Door recorder: copy-only, video-only 10-minute segments on the scratch volume behind the guard
Requirement: homehub-door-recorder.service (DOOR_RECORDER_ENABLED) shall run stack/door/door_recorder.py, which reads the relay once through ffmpeg in the pinned image (-c copy -an, MPEG-TS on stdout; the relay URL only in an ffconcat document on its stdin - never in argv, the container's environment or a file - built by the same helper as every SR-106 consumer) and itself cuts the stream into /srv/scratch/door/YYYY-MM-DD/door-YYYYmmddTHHMMSSZ.ts (UTC) at the first video keyframe (random_access_indicator) after each DOOR_RECORDER_SEGMENT_SEC (600) boundary, each file starting with the latest PAT and PMT. Before opening every segment it shall run the SR-103 guard and stop with exit 76 and an alert on a refusal; it shall prune whole oldest segments to stay under DOOR_RECORDER_CAP_MIB (7680) with room for the next; on EDQUOT/ENOSPC it shall stop with exit 75 and an alert (RestartPreventExitStatus); a segment ended by anything but a rotation shall be cut back to its last whole frame; a stall of DOOR_RECORDER_STALL_SEC ends the run for systemd to restart. `continuity` shall compute the downtime in a window (--hours back from now, or --since/--until) from the segments' names and PTS durations, the open .part included: the gaps between segments over 2 s and both uncovered edges of the window over 15 s (pass: at least one segment, at most 3 gaps and 5 minutes in all); `verify` shall decode segments with ffmpeg -v error.
Rationale: Plan W4b task 9. ffmpeg's own segment muxer opens the next file itself, between two guard checks, so the cut is made here, where the guard can run first. A frame cut short at a stop fails `ffmpeg -v error`, and the acceptance decodes one segment either side of every restart.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_door_relay.py on synthetic TS: PAT/PMT/PTS parsing, the packetiser realigning after junk and torn reads, cuts on keyframes with the header and on the clock, pruning whole oldest segments only, the guard before every segment and a refusal before opening, EDQUOT stopping with nothing written elsewhere, an interrupted segment cut back to its last whole frame, continuity (no segment, a short one in a long window and a trailing gap over 5 minutes all fail), UTC names, PTS duration. door-relay-lab.sh: every segment of three runs around a relay restart decodes with ffmpeg -v error and has no audio stream; continuity reports the restarts as gaps. Root suite: unmounted mid-run stops before the next file; a 4 MiB door quota gives EDQUOT, exit 75 and nothing outside door/.
Permutations: end={rotation; EOF; stop; EDQUOT; guard refusal}; stream={junk first; torn reads}

Title: Meeting recording: one state machine, and no indicator no capture
Requirement: With WALL_MEETING_RECORDING=true the wall image shall run wall-meeting-recorder.service (account wall-meeting, group audio, AF_UNIX only), which keeps one recording intent - idle, manual, call or manual-call - driven by the kiosk's start/stop requests (/run/wall-panel-renderer/meeting-request.json, each acted on once and only while under 30 s old) and by /run/wall-panel/call-state.json (state call or bridge, younger than 30 s) for the gateways named in WALL_MEETING_CALL_GATEWAYS (none named = the panel control only). A manual start during a call joins its recording (one file); a manual stop during a call stops it and suppresses the automatic trigger until that call ends (a call with a different `since` is a new call); repeated call notifications change nothing; the call ending stops a call recording and leaves a joined one recording as manual; a capture that fails or reaches its duration bound is finalised, the intent returns to idle and the current call is not re-triggered. Whenever the intent is not idle the recorder shall ask for the indicator (indicator true in /run/wall-meeting-recorder/state.json) and run the capture only while the kiosk's acknowledgement beats for the current sequence number (/run/wall-panel-renderer/meeting-indicator-ack.json) are under 1.0 s old, stopping it within 2 s of the indicator leaving the glass - the screen going dark, the kiosk going away, or the beats stopping (a beat counts only for the recording it names, and the kiosk samples the display for every beat, so its last beat is written at or before that moment); a manual start that sees no beat within 10 s is refused (indicator-unavailable), and a call waits without capturing. A lost indicator (a kiosk that crashes, freezes, reloads or goes dark) stops the capture, finalises the partial file and returns to idle, suppressing the automatic trigger for the call it was recording until that call ends. A recorder that restarts mid-recording finalises the partial file it left, starts idle, and remembers the call it was recording (or had suppressed) in /var/spool/wall-meeting/call-memory.json, keyed to the boot id, so the same call is not re-triggered after any restart of the unit while a reboot forgets it; a call with another `since` records automatically, and a manual start records the same call. A change of the selected microphone (the switch moving between Speaker and Headset) during a recording continues it in a new file.
Rationale: Ruled by the Owner 2026-10-22 (HomeHub open-items A69; OfficeWallNaglight WSN-097): both triggers, an on-screen indicator whenever capture runs, audio only, the Owner informs participants. "No indicator, no capture" is enforced by the absence of a message rather than by one: a kiosk that crashes, freezes, reloads or goes dark stops beating, so the capture stops with nothing having to work. This is the second explicit exception to SN-017's raw-audio rule, granted by the Owner for meetings only. A failed capture suppresses its call rather than retrying so that a broken ALSA leg cannot loop; the person can start it again by hand. A lost indicator and a recorder restart do the same (HomeHub plan 2026-10-22 W6 task 3: a recorder or kiosk crash finalises the partial file and returns to idle; Sol W6 review 1, F2): a recording never restarts itself after a failure the person did not see. The call memory lives in the spool, not the RuntimeDirectory, because that directory is removed on every stop so that a stopped recorder shows the kiosk nothing.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_wall_meeting_recorder.py TC-1400..TC-1402, TC-1404, TC-1405, TC-1407, TC-1408: every transition of the machine; no beat no capture; a beat for an older sequence number does not count; capture stops within 2 s of the last beat and within 2 s of the screen going dark over every phase of the beat and the poll (SIGINT, then SIGKILL after 0.4 s), while a modelled 500 ms display lag overruns it; a kiosk outage mid-call finalises one file and ends idle with no second capture while that call continues, and a manual start still records it; a recorder restarted mid-call finalises its partial, stays idle for the same `since` across restarts, forgets it at the call's end or a reboot, and records a new `since`; a manual start without an indicator gives up after 10 s; a crashed capture is finalised with its hash and the call is not retried; a crashed daemon's partial is finalised at the next start; unlisted gateways and an empty list record nothing automatically; a request from before a restart, or over 30 s old, is not acted on; the unit, the knobs (recording off unless true) and the firstboot block, executed. The kiosk half is OfficeWallNaglight TC-P-795..806.
Permutations: intent={idle; manual; call; manual-call}; event={manual start; manual stop; call up; repeated call; another call; call down; capture crash; duration bound; indicator lost; recorder restart; reboot}; gateway={listed; unlisted; none configured}; ack={none; older seq; fresh; stale}; request={new; repeated id; stale; from before a restart}; WALL_MEETING_RECORDING={unset; true; false; invalid}

Title: Meeting recording: both directions in one Opus file, inside hard bounds on the panel
Requirement: Each recording shall be one Ogg Opus file, stereo at WALL_MEETING_BITRATE_KBPS (default 48): left the near side, `mic_selected` resolved through /run/wall-panel/audio-mic-source.env as the call legs resolve it (the echo-cancelled panel microphone, or the headset's; with /run/wall-panel/audio-headset.env too, as wall-bt-call has it), so the input mute - the codec's capture switch - is honoured and records silence; right the far side, `bus_monitor` folded to mono, which is everything the panel plays including a Bluetooth call's far end; both opened as additional dsnoop readers. It is written to /var/spool/wall-meeting/recording/meeting-<UTC>.opus with every packet flushed, and finalised into ready/ with a <name>.sha256 sidecar written last; a partial left by a crash is finalised at the next start and a file with no audio is removed. The spool shall have a hard cap, WALL_MEETING_SPOOL_MAX_MB (512), and the root filesystem a free floor, WALL_MEETING_MIN_FREE_MB (5120): each capture runs with -fs set to the room left less 256 KiB and -t of WALL_MEETING_MAX_MINUTES (240); with under 4 MiB of room a start is refused as spool-full or disk-low, a call keeps its intent blocked and starts when room appears, and the state document carries the hub's quota as the hub last reported it (ok, full, or unknown after 15 minutes), so the kiosk can say when both are full.
Rationale: Measured on the panel 2026-10-22 with test tones (HomeHub FOLLOWUPS, W6 feasibility): mic_clean and bus_monitor read together alongside every existing consumer, during a live HFP call from the dev PC as well, at 4.9-5.5 % of one core for this ffmpeg command; a 2.7 kHz tone played on the bus rose 28 dB in the far channel and 12 dB in the near one. One stereo stream with a direction per channel is one encoder and one file any player opens, with both sides audible at once and still separable for the Owner's own review. ffmpeg checks -fs after writing and was measured 16 KiB past its limit, hence the margin. 48 kbit/s is about 21.6 MB an hour, so 512 MiB holds about 24 hours.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_wall_meeting_recorder.py TC-1403, TC-1406 and tests/test_meeting_transfer.py TC-1415: spool_room for each binding constraint; a full spool and a low disk refuse a manual start with the reason; the capture's -fs and -t come from the room and the knob; a capture ended on its limit is spool-full and blocks; a call blocked on a full spool starts when the hub drains it; a full hub and a full spool both reach the document; with real ffmpeg and generated tones the near tone lands on the left channel and the far tone on the right, -fs stops cleanly within the margin, and the recorder end to end records, stops within 2 s of the last beat and leaves a decodable file whose sidecar matches.
Permutations: room={plenty; under 4 MiB by cap; under 4 MiB by disk; over cap}; capture end={stopped; size limit; duration; crash}; hub={ok; full; stale}; mute={live; muted}; mode={bus; other}

Title: Meeting recordings leave the panel only by the hub pulling them, verified, then deleted
Requirement: The panel's wall-meeting account shall accept exactly one key, WALL_MEETING_PULL_PUBKEY (one ssh-ed25519 public key; empty or malformed = no key line), as restrict,command="/usr/local/lib/wall-panel/wall-meeting-spool", whose verbs are list (each finished recording with its size and sha256, oldest first), get NAME, ack NAME SHA256 (deletes only when the file's hash is SHA256; an absent file is already done) and report ok|full; anything else, or a NAME that is not a recording name, is refused with exit 2. The hub's homehub-meeting-pull (every 2 minutes, only when MEETING_PULL_ENABLED=true) shall run W4's scratch guard for `meetings` before the run and before every new file, stream each file into /srv/scratch/meetings/.incoming/NAME.part while hashing, and only when the size and the sha256 both match fsync it, rename it to /srv/scratch/meetings/YYYY-MM-DD/NAME and then ack it; an interrupted or oversize stream or a mismatched hash removes the part and leaves the panel's copy; a file already published with the same hash is acked again without a download; too little quota room (the smaller of statfs's free space and W4's quotactl reading of the meetings project), or EDQUOT/ENOSPC while writing, reports full to the panel, alerts and exits 75, and the next pull with room reports ok. ssh runs in batch mode with that key only, the panel's host key pinned on first contact in the pull's own known_hosts, and every call bounded.
Rationale: The scratch volume is in no share and must stay in none (HomeHub storage-map 3c), and the panel must not hold a credential that can write the hub, so the hub pulls. Publish-by-rename means a reader of meetings/ never sees a partial file under a final name; deleting on the panel only after the hub has the same bytes under the final name makes every step safe to repeat, so a timer retry is the whole recovery story. The public key travels in wall.env because it is not a secret; a hub reimage makes a new key, which is one wall.env line to follow (stack/meetings/README.md).
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_meeting_transfer.py TC-1409..TC-1412, TC-1414 and tests/test_wall_meeting_recorder.py TC-1408: the forced command refuses traversal, extra words, unknown verbs and long input, lists only sidecar-finished files, streams the bytes, deletes only on the matching hash and treats a repeated ack as done; a pull through the real Transport and the real spool script (an sshd stand-in) publishes by rename with nothing partial left and deletes on the panel after the ack; a truncated transfer is retried, a corrupted one keeps the panel's copy and alerts, a lost ack is repaired with no second download; an unreachable panel, a guard refusal (before the run or before a later file) and a full quota change nothing on the panel; firstboot writes the restricted key line and refuses a malformed key.
Permutations: verb={list; get; ack match; ack mismatch; ack absent; report; refused}; transfer={clean; truncated; corrupted; oversize; ack lost; already published; same name different hash}; guard={pass; refuse at start; refuse before a later file}; quota={room; no room; EDQUOT}; panel={reachable; unreachable}; key={valid; empty; malformed}

Title: Meeting recordings age out of the hub's 2 GiB quota
Requirement: homehub-meeting-retention (hourly, only when MEETING_PULL_ENABLED=true) shall, behind the scratch guard, delete recordings older than MEETING_RETENTION_DAYS (14, the proposed period; the Owner may change it) by the start time in their names, then the oldest while meetings/ holds more than MEETING_QUOTA_HIGH_PCT (90) of its quota as statfs reports it on the project directory, and partial transfers over an hour old, removing emptied day directories. --dry-run deletes nothing and prints each file it would; --days N overrides the period for a short dry run. Both hub units are scratch writers (RequiresMountsFor=/srv/scratch, BindsTo= and After=srv-scratch.mount, the guard as ExecStartPre, CapabilityBoundingSet=~CAP_SYS_RESOURCE, the knob as ExecCondition); firstboot installs both units and timers on every boot and enables the timers only for MEETING_PULL_ENABLED=true, making the pull key once and logging its public half; false or unset disables them; anything else changes nothing and warns.
Rationale: The ruling asks for short retention on scratch until the media drive exists. At ~21.6 MB an hour the 2 GiB quota holds about 99 hours, about 89 under the high-water, so 14 days fits about 6 hours of meetings a day; beyond that the high-water rule takes the oldest early instead of the quota refusing new ones. Hourly, because the high-water rule should act soon after a large pull. Not backed up and never shared (storage-map 3c).
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_meeting_transfer.py TC-1413, TC-1414: the period and the high-water rule (pure, with the cutoff kept); on a tree, an old recording and its day directory go and a new one stays, a stale partial goes and a fresh one stays; a short dry run deletes nothing and says what it would; a guard refusal deletes nothing; the arithmetic behind 14 days; both units carry the writer pattern; the timers' cadence; the knobs default off; the firstboot block, executed, for true, false, unset and invalid.
Permutations: age={inside the period; at the cutoff; past it}; usage={under high-water; over}; partial={fresh; stale}; run={real; dry; short dry}; guard={pass; refuse}; MEETING_PULL_ENABLED={unset; true; false; invalid}

Title: The frame-sync timer carries the Owner's 30-minute cadence, arms without a prior run, and replaces the panel's drop-in
Requirement: wall-sync-frame.timer shall trigger wall-sync-frame.service 30 minutes after the service last deactivated (OnUnitInactiveSec=30min, the Owner's cadence of 2026-09-15) and shall also carry a trigger that arms from the timer's own start (OnActiveSec=3min), so the first run happens without the service ever having run, at every boot and every resume. wall-firstboot.sh shall retire the drop-in wall-sync-frame.timer.d/10-cadence.conf only when its sha256 equals the Owner's 2026-09-15 file, leaving any other file under that directory in place and naming it in the journal, before it reloads systemd; and after enabling the timer it shall restart it if it is active but elapsed, and start it if it is not active.
Rationale: The Owner's drop-in reset the trigger list with an empty OnUnitInactiveSec= before setting 30min; systemd applies an empty assignment to the WHOLE list, so it also deleted OnBootSec=3min, and OnUnitInactiveSec alone never arms for a service that has never run. Measured on the panel 2026-10-22: SubState=elapsed, NextElapseUSecMonotonic=infinity, LastTriggerUSec empty, no wall-sync-frame journal entries (open-items C47); reproduced on systemd 255 in WSL. The same drop-in made the paired release of 2026-10-22 14:02 refuse (unit-has-dropin). daemon-reload does not re-arm an elapsed timer (measured), so the fixed unit alone would not fire on a running panel until a reboot.
AcceptanceCriteria: A test parses the shipped timer and asserts the effective trigger list, under systemd's reset semantics, is exactly OnActiveSec=3min and OnUnitInactiveSec=30min, with no OnUnitActiveSec, OnBootSec or Persistent; the same model applied to the old base plus the panel's byte-exact drop-in yields OnUnitInactiveSec alone and is judged unable to fire. firstboot's own retire function, run against real files, moves the byte-exact drop-in out and removes the empty directory, is a quiet no-op when it is absent, and leaves a different file of the same name and any other file in place with a journal line. firstboot's own arm function restarts an elapsed timer, leaves a waiting or running one alone, starts an inactive one, and fails the step when that fails. systemd-analyze verify accepts the unit pair. On the panel after a release: no DropInPaths, TimersMonotonic shows OnActiveUSec=3min and OnUnitInactiveUSec=30min, NextElapseUSecMonotonic finite, and a wall-sync-frame run in the journal; not yet run.
Permutations: dropin={owner-exact,absent,different,other-files,symlink}; timer={elapsed,waiting,running,inactive}; start={boot,resume,release,daemon-reload}

Title: OtterTube downloader: a daily, unit-owned, per-item ytdl-sub run on the scratch volume, images pinned by digest
Requirement: The repo shall provide stack/ottertube/: ottertube.py, the ytdl-sub presets (ytdl-sub/config.yaml), homehub-ottertube-download.service (oneshot) with its daily off-peak timer, homehub-ottertube-media.service, and compose services ottertube-ytdl-sub, ottertube-indexer and ottertube-media behind the `ottertube` profile, whose images are pinned by version and index digest in ottertube-images.pin and equal the OTTERTUBE_YTDL_SUB_IMAGE / OTTERTUBE_INDEXER_IMAGE knobs. The run shall start one ytdl-sub container per list item not already complete on the volume (its media, info.json and a completion marker written only after its checks passed; media left without the marker is checked again in place, any other leftover removed and fetched afresh; one-item subscription file, a polite pause between two downloads, none for a present item), then OtterTube's indexer, and write logs/last-run.json. OTTERTUBE_ENABLED, exactly `true`, is the switch: firstboot installs the three units always and enables the timer and media server only with it (disabling them otherwise), export-images bakes the two images only with it and refuses `ottertube` in COMPOSE_PROFILES, and the private list rides the site/ payload as an optional file.
Rationale: Plan W8c task 9 (the Owner 2026-10-22: deploy OtterTube with a curated catalogue). The kit (OtterTube deploy/hub) was never run against containers; its image's s6 init writes into /config and its cron runs every subscription in one process, so the guard could not run between items. Units that are BindsTo=srv-scratch.mount cannot sit enabled on a hub without the volume (systemd refuses to queue them: measured), so the knob gates the enable.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_ottertube.py: the pin equals the knobs; one subscription per item; present items cost no container; the pause only between downloads; units, timer, firstboot, bake and site-file contracts. Lab (ottertube-lab.sh): the pinned ytdl-sub fetches a real public-domain clip through the generated subscription under a read-only root with cap_drop ALL; a second run fetches nothing.
Permutations: knob={true; false; other}; item={absent; present}; scratch={present; absent}; COMPOSE_PROFILES={without; with ottertube}

Title: OtterTube's curated list is finite by construction and capped at 480p
Requirement: ottertube.py shall refuse (exit 2, alert, nothing changed) a list that is not version 1 of the documented schema, whose item URL is not https, carries a credential or a port, is on a host outside OTTERTUBE_ALLOWED_HOSTS, or does not match that host's single-item rule (a host with no rule cannot be used), whose item lacks a whole-number estimateMiB of 1..OTTERTUBE_MAX_FILESIZE_MIB or a recorded licence, source and https basis URL, whose collection has no valid bands or more than 25 items, whose items exceed OTTERTUBE_MAX_ITEMS, or whose estimates exceed OTTERTUBE_BUDGET_MIB; problems name ids and fields, never titles or URLs. Each item's subscription shall allow one download and yt-dlp a file of at most OTTERTUBE_MAX_FILESIZE_MIB, and a downloaded video whose real height (ffprobe of the pinned image) is over 480 or unreadable shall be discarded with all its files.
Rationale: Plan W8c task 10: every subscription finite (fixed items, never everything), at most 480p, sized well inside the 6 GiB quota, and only sources whose terms permit download. A host allow-list plus a per-host single-item rule makes 'one video' a property of the code, and a source added without review a refusal. A bare file URL declares no height (measured), so the cap is checked on the file.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_ottertube.py: a good list's plan; each refusal by name; YouTube only with the Owner's host entry and only a watch URL without a list; problems carry no title or URL; a 720p file and an unreadable height are discarded. Lab: the real clip is H.264 at 240p.
Permutations: url={single; channel; playlist; search; http; credential; port; unknown host; host without rule}; estimate={ok; missing; over cap; bool}; total={within budget; over}; height={<=480; >480; unreadable}

Title: OtterTube's catalogue: OtterTube's own indexer, a hard-linked publication, the list's titles, pruning
Requirement: After the items, ottertube.py shall write approved.json from the list (one entry per collection: folder and id = the collection id, the list's title, bands and order) into the work directory and run OtterTube's indexer (tools/catalog/build-catalog.mjs from the recorded OtterTube commit, in the pinned node image, no network) with --require-hardlink and --allow-missing (and --allow-shrink only when the list itself names fewer items than the served catalogue and at least half of them are complete, so a deliberate removal reaches the catalogue and downloads that go missing keep the indexer's protection) over /library (downloads and publication in one bind, so the publication is hard links and costs no second copy) to /catalog/catalog.json. Before indexing it shall set each new item's info.json title to the list's, fetch the list's thumbnail when the source gave none (https, allowed host, at most 4 MiB, by rename), and delete the files of items and collections the list no longer names (never following a link). An indexer failure leaves the previous catalogue served and alerts.
Rationale: Plan W8c task 9. The catalogue must be built by the validator the app itself uses, so OtterTube's indexer runs unchanged. A bare file URL's title is its file name (measured), so the list carries the title children see.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_ottertube.py: approved.json shape, accepted by OtterTube's own checkApproved (cross-repo); the indexer argv; titles and the thumbnail; pruning, and no link followed. Lab: the real indexer publishes the real clip as a hard link (one inode) and the catalogue names it.
Permutations: item={new; present; removed}; collection={kept; removed}; thumb={from source; from list; none}; indexer={ok; fails}

Title: OtterTube follows the scratch writer rules: a guard before every container, a clean stop on EDQUOT or ENOSPC
Requirement: The download unit and the media server unit shall carry RequiresMountsFor=/srv/scratch, BindsTo=srv-scratch.mount, CapabilityBoundingSet=~CAP_SYS_RESOURCE and an ExecCondition on the knob; the download unit runs the scratch guard as ExecStartPre and ottertube.py runs it again before the run, before every item's container and before the indexer, a refusal stopping the run (exit 76, alert) with nothing further done on the volume, not even the cleanup of work/; every cleanup of work/ after the start of the run shall first check that the mounted volume is still the scratch volume (the guard's checks, a write probe failing only because the budget is full excepted) and leave work/ as it is when it is not. After any non-zero exit of a run container's client (a timeout, a missing client or the container's own failure) the named container shall be removed and confirmed gone before anything else runs; when it cannot be confirmed, the run stops (exit 1, alert ottertube-container) and starts nothing further. The compose services shall have restart "no", read-only root filesystems, cap_drop ALL (the media server adds back only NET_BIND_SERVICE, which its binary carries as a file capability), no-new-privileges, no log driver and long-syntax binds with create_host_path: false, none of them at /lib, and bind only /srv/scratch/ottertube/ of the volume. EDQUOT or ENOSPC, in a container's output or raised by ottertube.py, shall stop the run with exit 75: the work directory emptied, an alert through homehub-alert.sh, logs/last-run.json result `quota`, no further item attempted and nothing written elsewhere.
Rationale: IF-071 and plan W4a: a missing volume must never redirect writes onto /, and a runaway download must stop at its own quota without touching door/ or meetings/ (plan W8c task 10's oversized-item test). Binding a volume at /lib shadows the image's loader (measured: nothing in the container could start). The caddy binary in the image carries cap_net_bind_service as a file capability, which the kernel refuses to exec without it in the bounding set (measured).
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_ottertube.py: guard before the run, every item and the indexer; refusals before the run and before the second item leave an existing work/ tree untouched, and a cleanup whose guard refuses leaves it too; EDQUOT and ENOSPC in output, and EDQUOT raised here, stop with 75; another OSError is not mistaken for it; the compose contract. Root suite under the hub's kernel (ottertube-quota.root-test.sh): an oversized item stops at EDQUOT, door/ and meetings/ still write, ottertube is writable again; unmounted before and mid-run, exit 76 with nothing under the bare mount point. Lab: the real ytdl-sub's ENOSPC on a full filesystem stops the run with 75.
Permutations: guard={passes; refuses before run; refuses mid-run}; write={ok; EDQUOT; ENOSPC; other error}; mount={present; absent; lost mid-run}

Title: OtterTube served on one LAN-only name: the web build, the catalogue and the publication with range requests
Requirement: Caddy shall serve {$OTTERTUBE_HOST} (OTTERTUBE_SUBDOMAIN, default ottertube, under DOMAIN) with the dns-01 issuer, behind the @lan remote_ip gate (403 otherwise) and no login: /ottertube/ from ./ottertube/web (OtterTube's dist/web, read-only), /ottertube/catalog.json (no-cache) and /ottertube/media/<video|music>/<id>.<media or image ext> (no-cache) proxied to homehub-ottertube-media, a read-only file server of the publication and the catalogue bound to the volume; anything else under media/ is 404; CORS only for https://{$OTTERTUBE_HOST} and app://ottertube; / serves the update channel's landing page (SR-125), which links to /ottertube/. Range requests shall answer 206. provision-technitium.sh shall create the name's pinpoint record only while the site knob is on (SR-126: OTTERTUBE_SITE_ENABLED, empty following OTTERTUBE_ENABLED), never a wildcard. `ottertube.py status` reports the last run, the catalogue's age and the library's size (each inode once) for deployment-state.
Rationale: Plan W8c task 9: one name, LAN-only (auto-memory hub-lan-only-dns: a Primary pinpoint zone per name, no wildcard), one new certificate. A separate media server keeps the main Caddy from ever binding the scratch volume: a missing volume stops it, not every site, and the door's recordings are never inside the proxy's view.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_ottertube.py: the Caddy block, the provision record guarded by the knob, serve-check, status counting a hard link once. Lab with the real block (TLS internal): catalogue 200 no-cache; media Range 0-99 = 206 with Content-Range; CORS for app://ottertube only; an info.json and a dot file 404; / the landing page (since 2026-10-27; it was a 302) and the web build 200; a client outside LAN_CIDR 403.
Permutations: path={web; catalogue; media; info.json; dot file; /}; origin={site; app; other}; client={LAN; off-LAN}; range={none; 0-99}; knob={true; false}

Title: The nightly hub backup reports its verified success to the unified backup lane as nightlySuccess
Requirement: Each nightly config backup run (backup.sh) that finishes verified and promoted (the backup ok path, after retention) shall POST exactly one body {id,nightlySuccess:<RFC3339 UTC, trailing Z>} to the unified backup-state endpoint through post_file_share_backup_state, with the shared bearer. A failed, refused or missing run shall post nothing, so the age of the last nightlySuccess grows. A lost post shall be a warning, never a failure of the backup. The run shall never write lastSuccess, shareHealth or runState. The nightly run archives the hub's own data and does not send offsite.
Rationale: The household has one backup indicator (the File Backups row). Owner decision 2026-10-23: the hub's own nightly backup must turn that row non-green when it stops succeeding, without any producer writing another's field.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/nightly-success-feed.test.sh: success posts one nightlySuccess body with the bearer on both transports; every failure path posts nothing; a non-200 or unanswered post warns and returns 0; an unset URL skips; a malformed value is refused locally; backup.sh has exactly one success report on the backup ok path. Rollout: tracker support first, then this producer; no backfill; the tracker must not be rolled back to a version without the field once this producer is live (the old writer drops the unknown key on save).
Permutations: outcome={success; failure; refused/unanswered post; URL unset}; transport={curl; docker exec wget}

Title: The hub records a 5-minute metrics snapshot, kept a year
Requirement: homehub-metrics-snapshot.timer (every 5 min, on the clock) shall append one JSON line to /var/lib/homehub-metrics/snapshot-YYYYMMDD.jsonl (UTC day) holding: every gauge as the tracker's /api/today serves it (value, range, target, observed_at, the computed stale flag and colour), read ONLY as HOMEHUB_METRICS_USER from a loopback URL with the tracker bearer token, and with a blank user nothing requested; the newest homehub-telemetry sample; memory and uptime; every container's state, health and restart count; every homehub-*.service's last result and every failed unit; the watch/disk/liveness verdicts and the meeting pull's last run; a summary of the wall panel's telemetry, disk check and freeze watchdog pulled with the meeting pull's key through the panel's forced command (verb status, never accepting a host key); and NVMe SMART once an hour. Each block that fails is recorded as {ok:false,error} and costs nothing else. Record only: it alerts, starts and stops nothing, and runs as its own unit (not the 30 s telemetry sampler) with one run deadline inside TimeoutStartSec. Retention: 365 day files, gzip'd after 7, a day file capped at 16 MiB and the record at 1 GiB, the active file never deleted or compressed. On the hub it is in no config backup and never under the tracker's data folder.
Rationale: The Owner asked on 2026-10-26 for the gauge parameters and hardware/service status every 5 minutes, for trend charts and for debugging by the Owner and agents (HomeHub open-items A79, plan HUB_METRICS_LOG_PLAN_2026-10-26). Nothing kept the gauges as the wall saw them, service status over time, or the panel's own short-lived telemetry. Title: The hub writes a daily row at 10:00 and a revision at 14:05
Requirement: homehub-metrics-daily.timer (OnCalendar 10:00 and 14:05 America/Chicago, Persistent=true) shall append to /var/lib/homehub-metrics/daily.jsonl one row per due kind for the night that ended on that local date: kind initial from 10:00, revision from 14:05, each only when no row of that kind exists for the night (a catch-up after 14:05 writes both; nothing is back-filled for an earlier night). A row carries every gauge with value, target, unit, observed_at and stale, the list of gauges with no believable reading (missing), the heart feeder's night summary, the CPAP usage minutes and sleep score, the overnight (22:00-08:00 local) CPU and NVMe temperature range from the telemetry record, the backup units' results, its written_at, scheduled time and a late flag (more than 30 min after its time). Both rows are kept; a reader takes the latest per night. Kept for ever (64 MiB cap).
Rationale: The Owner ruled 2026-10-26 (A79 decisions 3.1, 3.2): sleep lands about 06:00-06:15 but has been corrected later in the day, and the heart gauge gives up on a night at 14:00 (LLR-1319), so a 10:00 row alone would show nights as missing that arrived later.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_hub_metrics.py TC-1499, TC-1500: due kinds at 09:59/10:00/14:04/14:05/15:00, across DST and UTC midnight, no back-fill; the timer's OnCalendar lines equal the code's zone and times; a row's gauges, missing list, heart night, CPAP minutes, score, overnight range and backup results; a repeat run writes nothing and 14:05 adds the revision marked late when caught up; an unreadable tracker is recorded as gauges_error.
Permutations: time={before 10:00; 10:00; 14:04; 14:05; catch-up after 14:05; next morning}; zone={CDT; CST fall-back day}; tracker={read; unreadable}; telemetry={in window; outside}

Title: OtterTube's update channel: three exact names served byte for byte from a folder of its own
Requirement: Caddy's {$OTTERTUBE_HOST} block shall serve /ottertube/update.json and /ottertube/update.json.sig (Cache-Control no-cache) and /ottertube/OtterTube-<7 lowercase hex>.exe from stack/ottertube/updates, mounted read-only at /srv/ottertube/updates into caddy and into no other service, with no encode on any of them and ahead of the web build's catch-all; /ottertube/update-<linux|darwin|windows>-<x64|arm64>.json and its .sig shall be routed the same way (reserved for later platforms; update.json stays the Windows schema-1 file). No other name in the folder shall be reachable. The site's root / (with /landing.js and /landing.css) shall be a static landing page from stack/ottertube/landing (git-tracked, mounted read-only, Content-Security-Policy default-src 'none' with only same-origin script, style and fetch) whose script reads update.json and offers a download link to the exe it names with its version and build date, inserting every manifest value as text, shows 'No release published yet' on a 404 and no link for any manifest OtterTube would refuse, and carries the SmartScreen install note (the exe has no Authenticode signature). The folder ships with a README only and is not backed up.
Rationale: Plan OTTERTUBE_UPDATE_CHANNEL 2026-10-26 section 3 (the Owner's rulings 5.1, 5.3, 5.6). OtterTube's client (desktop/src/main/update.ts) checks an ed25519 signature over the manifest's exact bytes and the exe's Content-Length, size and SHA-256, so any re-encoding or re-formatting breaks every update; web/ is replaced by rsync --delete on each web-build delivery, so the channel cannot live there.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_ottertube_updates.py: the mount, the exact handles without encode, the order, the reserved names, the names agreeing with OtterTube's client and manifest maker. Lab with the real block (TLS internal): update.json and its .sig 200, no-cache, the folder's exact bytes and Content-Length and no Content-Encoding with gzip/br/zstd offered, not a decoy in web/; the exe likewise and Range 206; near-miss names, a .tmp and the README not served; the reserved name served; the web build still encoded; / is the tracked landing page with its CSP, catalog.json still proxied. Node: the landing script links exactly the published exe as text, and shows no link for 404, errors or a refused manifest; in headless Edge the link is not displayed before the script, on a 404, an error or a refused manifest, and is for the published release, with no CSP violation.
Permutations: file={update.json; update.json.sig; exe; reserved; near miss; README; .tmp}; Accept-Encoding={none; gzip,br,zstd}; decoy in web/={yes}

Title: Hub camera motion detector: the event source for motion clips, the panel's pinned engine, off until a measured cost test
Requirement: homehub-camera-motion@<camera>.service (one per CAMERAS name; ExecCondition CAMERA_<C>_MOTION_ENABLED, shipped false) shall run stack/camera-motion/camera_motion.py, which runs motion_engine.py - OfficeWallNaglight doorstream/motion.py at the commit in motion-engine.pin with its comments removed and two docstrings made neutral (this repository is public: the Owner, 2026-10-27) and its code unchanged, refusing (exit 78, an alert, RestartPreventExitStatus) when the file is not the pinned sha256 - on a decode of the camera's go2rtc relay stream built by door_relay.relay_consumer (the credential only on the decoder's stdin; never a connection to the camera), with the panel's own raster filter `fps=<sample_fps>,scale=256:256:flags=area,format=gray` (software) or, by CAMERA_<C>_MOTION_DECODE=vaapi, VA-API decode and scale_vaapi on the iGPU; the arrival clock time.monotonic() as on the panel; OpenCV single-threaded. The engine's knobs are CAMERA_<C>_MOTION_* parsed by the engine's own motion_config; a configuration MotionConfig.eligible refuses (the whole-image placeholder zone, not calibrated) is refused (78). Each new event (approach, road-stop) shall be written at once as an IF-076 record; renewals (visitor, bridge, road-hold) at most every 3 s, and the last renewal of an episode always, so the written records reproduce the panel's display window. `replay` shall run the same engine over recorded segments (every Kth frame by index, -fps_mode passthrough) and `cost` shall measure the decoder container and the unit against CAMERA_MOTION_BUDGET_PCT (25 % of one core). python3-opencv is in the hub's packages.list and installed by firstboot when a camera's motion knob is true.
Rationale: Source: the Owner, 2026-10-26 (HomeHub open-items A78, closed with its rulings; plan docs/MEDIA_DRIVE_AND_CAMERA_CLIPS_PLAN_2026-10-26.md section 0). The panel's detector runs only while the panel is lit and the office occupied, so as the only source it would make no clips at night or with the office empty. One engine, pinned, so the hub and the panel cannot disagree about what is motion; the zones stay private (MiniPC-Deployer is public). Measured 2026-10-22: a 5 fps 256x256 grey decode from the relay costs 17.7 % of one core; 2026-10-27 on the hub: VA-API decode with scale_vaapi about a third of the software decode's CPU, with a different raster (mean 4 grey levels apart), hence a knob switched only after replay agrees.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_camera_motion.py: the engine is the pinned bytes and an edited copy is refused; its syntax tree, docstrings aside, equals the pinned commit's in the sibling checkout, and it carries no comment and no date; the knobs reach the engine's parser and a placeholder refuses without printing a polygon; the decoder carries the credential only on stdin and its filter is the panel's motion_filter character for character; the spooler writes events at once, throttles renewals without leaving a hole the cutter would split on, and keeps the last; the REAL engine on synthetic frames yields one unbroken episode; replay selects by index without retiming; the cost verdict; the knob condition; a refusal alerts and starts no decoder; no private zone anywhere in the public tree. On the hub (deploy): cost at or under 25 % of one core over 30 min.
Permutations: decode={software; vaapi}; zones={private; placeholder; malformed}; engine={pinned; edited}; signal={event; renewal; last renewal}; knob={true; false; unlisted}

Title: Motion clips cut copy-only from the rolling recording, by event time, to the panel's display window
Requirement: homehub_clips.py `cut` (homehub-clips-cut.timer, every minute after the last run; CLIPS_ENABLED) shall read the IF-076 store for each camera in CAMERAS (CAMERA_<C>_SOURCES) and group records into episodes: an `event` whose cause is in CAMERA_<C>_CLIP_CAUSES (approach road-stop) opens one; every record at or before its end extends it to that record + CAMERA_<C>_CLIP_LEASE_SEC (5); an episode reaching CAMERA_<C>_CLIP_MAX_SEC (600) continues as a `continued` clip with no pre-roll. The window is CAMERA_<C>_CLIP_PRE_SEC (3) before the first event to the episode's end. Once the window has closed (+15 s) and the recording has reached its end (or 180 s have passed), it shall be cut from the recorder's segments: each segment's frames indexed by the recorder's TS parser, timed by name + PTS offset or, when the PTS is not believable, by index at CAMERA_<C>_FPS; from the last keyframe at or before the window start (at most 5 s back) to before the first frame at or after its end; an open .ts.part read only to its last frame start; the bytes (with the file's PAT/PMT before a mid-file start) piped to ffmpeg in the relay's pinned image, -c copy -an, MP4 +faststart, written as .mp4.part; timestamps regenerated (setts N/(fps*TB)) only for index timing or a PTS discontinuity; verified by ffprobe to hold exactly the planned frames before the rename. Names and records are IF-077. A window no segment covers is recorded lost (pruned, or no recording) and alerted once per run; a failed cut is retried twice, then recorded; an episode whose core overlaps one already cut is not cut again.
Rationale: Source: the Owner, 2026-10-26 (HomeHub open-items A78, closed with its rulings; plan docs/MEDIA_DRIVE_AND_CAMERA_CLIPS_PLAN_2026-10-26.md section 0). The Owner's window: 3 s pre-roll, then the panel's own display window (5 s after presence ends, or a 30 s hold for a stopped vehicle, WSN-107) - which the detector's renewals carry, so no separate post-roll or merge numbers. Copy-only from the NVMe rolling segments (~27 h). Measured 2026-10-26: the camera sometimes sends a whole segment with 0.07 s of PTS (6000 frames), so timing falls back to the frame index.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_hub_clips.py on synthetic TS (the recorder's fixture): the frame index, PTS and index timing (wrap; broken PTS); episodes (extension, orphans, the max-length continuation); the plan (keyframe snap, end, a mid-file start with the header, a segment's first frame from its first byte, a restart's gap and regeneration, an open .part, an uncovered start or end); readiness and loss; the cut feeds exactly the planned bytes and publishes a verified clip, a short or failed cut is removed; the ledger cuts each episode once, an overlapping second source does not recut, a loss alerts; retries. TC-1569 (release tier): real recorded segments cut into clips that decode with the planned frames.
Permutations: timing={pts; index}; boundary={continuous; restart; gap}; window={inside; across segments; open .part; partly pruned; pruned}; result={cut; short; ffmpeg failed; quota}

Title: Clips re-encoded on the iGPU in a low-priority batch, the copy kept as the fallback
Requirement: homehub_clips.py `encode` (homehub-clips-encode.timer, every 15 min; only while CLIPS_ENCODE_ENABLED=true, shipped false) shall re-encode at most CLIPS_ENCODE_MAX_PER_RUN clips whose sidecar has no encode result, oldest first, with h264_vaapi or hevc_vaapi (CLIPS_ENCODE_CODEC) at VBR CLIPS_ENCODE_KBPS (peak twice that) in the relay's pinned image, the container at --cpu-shares 2 and the unit at Nice 19 with idle I/O; never inline with the cut. The encoded file replaces the copy only when ffprobe counts the copy's frames (within one) and it is at most CLIPS_ENCODE_KEEP_PCT (80) of the copy's size; otherwise, and on any failure, the copy stays. The sidecar's `encode` records the outcome either way (a clip is tried once) and its bytes and sha256 follow the file kept. A full quota stops the batch as it stops the cutter.
Rationale: Source: the Owner, 2026-10-26 (HomeHub open-items A78, closed with its rulings; plan docs/MEDIA_DRIVE_AND_CAMERA_CLIPS_PLAN_2026-10-26.md section 0). Measured 2026-10-27 on the hub (UHD 600, iHD 25.4.6): a 30 s daytime window copy 2.31 MB; VBR 300 kb/s 1.09 MB, 450 kb/s 1.68 MB; constant QP 30 was LARGER than the copy (the camera's own daylight stream is lean) - hence a bitrate target and the keep rule. Encode CPU 1.3-2.1 s per 60 s of video.
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_hub_clips.py: the encoder's arguments (VA-API, VBR, hevc's hvc1 tag, the lowest CPU weight, no stdin); a verified smaller encode replaces the copy and the sidecar follows; a larger one, a frame-count mismatch or a failed ffmpeg keeps the copy and records why; a full quota stops the batch. On the hub (deploy): size and CPU over a day of clips before the knob is turned on.
Permutations: codec={h264; hevc}; result={kept; larger; frames differ; ffmpeg failed; quota}

Title: Motion clips storage: a guarded, quota-capped area, 1 year capped at 100 GB
Requirement: Clips shall be written only under CLIPS_ROOT: /srv/scratch/clips (the scratch volume's `clips` quota project 7104, 1 GiB, sized before ottertube so ottertube gives up the room first; IF-071's guard as writer `clips`) or /srv/media/Clips (a separate ext4 mount with prjquota, writable; the drive's identity check is the media-drive build's); any other value is refused. The guard shall run before every file the cut, encode and retention write, and their units drop CAP_SYS_RESOURCE. EDQUOT/ENOSPC shall stop the pipeline (exit 75, an alert, a stop marker): no further cut or encode until `retention` (hourly) finds the quota under CLIPS_QUOTA_HIGH_PCT and lifts it. Retention shall delete clips (mp4 and sidecar together) older than CLIPS_RETENTION_DAYS (365), then oldest first while the total exceeds CLIPS_CAP_MIB (95367 = 100 GB, the cap winning over the age), then while the clips project is past CLIPS_QUOTA_HIGH_PCT (90) until 5 points under; rewrite each camera's index without them; remove .part files over an hour old, empty day folders and event-store days past CLIPS_EVENT_DAYS (14). `status` reports per camera the newest event and clip, counts, the encode backlog and the detector's status file. One run of cut, encode or retention at a time (a lock). firstboot installs every unit, enables a detector instance per CAMERAS name, provisions python3-opencv before starting them when a camera's knob is true, and converges the clip timers to CLIPS_ENABLED and CLIPS_ENCODE_ENABLED.
Rationale: Source: the Owner, 2026-10-26 (HomeHub open-items A78, closed with its rulings; plan docs/MEDIA_DRIVE_AND_CAMERA_CLIPS_PLAN_2026-10-26.md section 0). Retention 1 year capped at 100 GB, the cap winning; the media drive is not bought yet (C111), so a small quota-capped area on the NVMe scratch first, switched to /srv/media/Clips by a knob later. The 18 GB scratch volume stays; its usable space is fully budgeted, so the clips quota comes out of ottertube's ceiling (5882 -> 4858 MiB granted on the live hub; ottertube uses under 1 GiB of a 3 GiB list budget).
AcceptanceCriteria: tests/test_hub_clips.py: the scratch `clips` writer judged with project 7104 and refused with another project or CAP_SYS_RESOURCE; the media guard's refusals; the reduction order and the live volume's numbers; retention's age, cap and quota rules and their order; pairs removed, the index rewritten, stale parts and old event days removed; the quota stop holds the cutter until retention makes room and is set by a quota hit with an alert; status; the units, the firstboot block and the template. scratch-fs.root-test.sh check 7: clips stops at its quota.
Permutations: root={scratch; media; other}; age={within; beyond}; total={under cap; over cap}; quota={under; past high}; knobs={off; clips on; encode on}
